mergedPulls.title: server(2017): assert event-loop yield by ordering, not wall-clock ms, in the attachment-gc test
mergedPulls.body:
## What

`apps/server/test/attachment-gc.test.ts` now asserts the event-loop yield of the attachment-gc tick by ordering, not by wall-clock milliseconds. The concurrent `/api/projects` request must settle while the gc sweep is still working through the 200k-row corpus, checked as the absence of the `attachment gc:` completion log line before the response arrives. #2017 reports the previous bounds (`tickMs < 100`, window `< 250` ms) failing on the shared host at load 40-44 with measured 327/334 ms: the bounds measured the machine, not the code.

Test-only change. `scheduler.ts` and `attachment-gc.ts` are untouched. A lessons ledger entry records the error kind (`docs/lessons/2017-wall-clock-bound-in-shared-host-test.md`).

## Verified

Red: with `advanceGc` patched to drain the batch generator synchronously in a `while` loop (a fully blocking tick), the test fails at the ordering assertion, `AssertionError: expected true to be false`, because the completion line `attachment gc: 0 pending, 1 orphan, 8 bytes reclaimed` is logged before the response settles. Full output: [negative-control.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/eec2b6cb/docs/verify/2017/negative-control.txt), committed on this branch.

Green: with the batched implementation (one 128-row batch per `setImmediate` turn), `cd apps/server && npx vitest run test/attachment-gc.test.ts` passes 15/15 in 4.2s, and stays green under 8 concurrent CPU busy-loop processes (exit 0, 15/15). `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm prepush` (26 checks, including the affected e2e set) pass on the pushed HEAD `eec2b6cb`.

## Upstream

No mechanism is added; the change rewrites assertions in one repo test.

## Risk

Test-only, two-way door (revert one block). The ordering assertion still fails when the tick blocks the loop (negative control above), but it no longer bounds per-batch latency: a regression that only slows each batch without blocking the loop is no longer caught by this test. The EXPLAIN and index-usage assertions in the same file keep the scan bounded. Blast radius is this one test file; the full-file run and prepush cover it.

## Acceptance

- [x] The test fails when the tick is made fully synchronous: the negative-control run is red at the ordering assertion, output committed at `docs/verify/2017/negative-control.txt` and linked in Verified.
- [x] No absolute wall-clock bound remains in this test: `grep -n "performance.now\|toBeLessThan" apps/server/test/attachment-gc.test.ts` returns zero matches.
- [x] `cd apps/server && npx vitest run test/attachment-gc.test.ts` passes (15/15), also under 8 concurrent CPU busy loops.

## Issues

Closes #2017.

## What

Chat parity T6 (#2009). The home is one Chief chat for every project in the team, and #1923 taught the Chief to investigate and pick a project. This PR gives the user the controls around that choice.

- Composer project chip (`apps/web/src/chief/chief-conversation.tsx`, shared menu `apps/web/src/chief/project-menu.tsx`). It shows only when the team has two or more projects. The menu `发给哪个项目` lists `自动` plus each project with its description. The pick is remembered per browser.
- `@` in the Chief composer: picking a project row from the existing inline mention list sets the chip and removes the `@query` text (`acceptInlineRow` in `apps/web/src/overlay/composer-wire.ts`, now also used by the detail composer).
- `POST /api/teams/:id/chief/threads` and `POST /api/conversations/:id/messages` accept an optional `projectId`. The server checks it belongs to the team (400 otherwise) and prefixes the Chief prompt with `【输入框选定项目：name（id: …）】`. The stored message stays as typed.
- Chief prompt (`composeChiefSystemPrompt`): a chip pick wins with no investigation or question; a project question lists the tied candidates plus `都不是`; a misplaced unstarted todo is moved with `update_todo`.

The todo goes to the end of the target column, its schedule follows, old tags are dropped (tags sent with the move must belong to the target). A self-created GitHub issue is re-created in the new repo; only after that succeeds is the old one closed as not planned with a comment linking the new issue. If the new repo refuses, the old issue stays open and linked, and the existing retry endpoint finishes the replacement. Moving to a project without GitHub closes the old issue right away. An imported GitHub issue, a started todo and a todo in another team are refused.

mergedPulls.title: daemon+server(1786): retry provider network failures before model fallback
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Before: on 2026-10-26 Cairn builds for #1617 and #1618 failed four times on transient errors. pi's `Connection error.` from the model provider was logged as `retryable=false` and failed the whole build with no retry and no fallback; a relay `503 All available accounts exhausted` failed a build although the agent had fallback models; a `git push` connection reset failed a build with the work only local. Each one needed a person to restart the build.

After: plan and build steps that fail on a provider network error (`Connection error`, `ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `fetch failed`) retry the same model after 2s, 4s, 8s and 16s, then move through `fallbackModels`. Provider outages (5xx, "exhausted") and capacity limits also trigger fallback. Git network operations, the closing push included, retry transient failures with the same backoff. The step fails only when the chain is exhausted.

This builds on the orchestration lane's unreviewed partial work (git retries and outage fallback triggers) and finishes it.

## Verified

Tests written first and red on main: `apps/daemon/test/runner-network-retry.test.ts` (Connection error retried, then fallback), `apps/server/test/model-fallback.test.ts` (503 exhausted moves to the next model), `apps/daemon/test/git.test.ts` (push retried twice after resets, then succeeds).

```
[prepush] PASS (22 checks)
```

## Upstream

Reuses `withGitNetRetries`, the existing fallback chain (`fallbackModels`, #1506) and `classifyStepFailure`.

## Risk

Two-way door. A real outage now takes up to about 30 seconds per model before the step fails, instead of failing at once. Non-provider failures (git errors, context or tool-budget exhaustion) no longer count as provider outages, and git network retries keep main's retry-by-default semantics, short-circuiting only auth, 403/404, TLS and push-hook failures.

## Acceptance

- [x] A step whose first model answers 503 exhausted continues on the fallback model and succeeds.
- [x] A push that fails twice with a connection reset and then succeeds does not fail the build.

mergedPulls.title: server+web(1938): keep the chief reachable when its model is down or busy
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU?thread=cmsg_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU6c1oaT385ZfmHMzJjUfw6z)_

## What

Keeps the chief chat usable when the chief's model is down and while the chief is mid-reply (tickets T4 and T5 of the home chat redesign, #1938).

When the chief is down, a banner above the composer says why, when it retries, and that tasks keep running. It offers two actions: change the chief's model, or create a task directly. On a phone it collapses to one line with a details toggle. Messages sent meanwhile stay as held bubbles that can be withdrawn, and they run in order once the chief is back. When a backup model answers, the model row shows an orange dot with screen-reader text, and each reply carries a "answered by backup model X" note.

While the chief is replying, new messages show as queued with two actions: steer now, or withdraw. Steering feeds the message into the running turn. The stop square shows only when the chief is busy and the input is empty. A stopped turn leaves a row that says no task was created, or links the tasks created before the stop.

Server side:
- `apps/server/src/services/chief-turns.ts` holds the per-thread queue, steer, stop, withdraw and outage logic.
- A chief step id equals its user message id, so the queue maps to messages without a migration.
- Chief steps on one thread are claimed strictly in order (`hasEarlierLiveChiefStep` in `machine-claim.ts`).
- Chief steps join the model fallback chain, but only to models on the same runtime.
- A steer counts as delivered only after the daemon acks it; until then the message keeps its queued turn.
- New routes: `DELETE .../chief/threads/:tid/messages/:mid`, `POST .../messages/:mid/steer` and `POST .../chief/threads/:tid/stop`.

![outage desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/4496910c/docs/verify/1938/outage-desktop.png)
![outage phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/4496910c/docs/verify/1938/outage-phone.png)
![queued](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/4496910c/docs/verify/1938/queued.png)
![fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/4496910c/docs/verify/1938/fallback.png)
![stopped with task](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/4496910c/docs/verify/1938/stopped-with-task.png)

## Verified

The server tests and e2e specs are new files written before the code. On the old code the routes did not exist, and the specs failed on missing test ids. On this branch:

```
apps/server: vitest run test/chief-queue-steer-stop.test.ts
      Tests  18 passed (18)
apps/server full suite: 405 files, 5433 passed
apps/web: playwright test e2e/chief-home-busy.spec.ts
  10 passed (14.7s)
full e2e (e2e:affected fell back to the full suite): 1311 passed
chief-home-chat, chief-panel, chief-stream-markdown: passed
pnpm typecheck: Done for shared, daemon, web, server, integration
biome ci: Checked 1032 files, no fixes applied
spec-parse-gate: PASS, 1311 tests in 186 files
```

The fallback runtime filter has a negative control: with the filter removed, the "different-runtime fallback is skipped" case goes red.

## Upstream

This uses the existing step queue, `steerPending`/`stopPending` tables, machine signals and `planModelFallback` already in this repo. No new dependency.

## Risk

Two-way door: no migration, and the new rows are system messages that older clients ignore.

Blast radius is the chief conversation and step claiming. Worker steps are unchanged except for the shared fallback code, which is covered by the full server suite above.

A steered message stays queued until the daemon calls `POST /api/machine/steer/ack` after handing the text to the live session. A daemon older than this PR never acks, so its steered messages also run as their own turn after the current one ends. That is a repeat, never a loss.

Known limits, left as is:
- A rewind turn gets a new step id, so it is not listed as pending or withdrawable.
- `listChiefThreads` and the chief claim loop run a few more queries per thread. The thread counts are small.

## Acceptance

- [x] Outage banner shows reason, retry time and both actions; phone collapses to one line (`chief-home-busy.spec.ts`, outage screenshots)
- [x] Messages sent during an outage are held, withdrawable and replayed in order (server test "held messages stay in order and resume in order", e2e withdraw case)
- [x] Backup model marked with a dot, screen-reader text and a per-reply note (e2e fallback case, fallback screenshot)
- [x] Messages sent while busy are queued with steer and withdraw (e2e queued and steer cases, queued screenshot)
- [x] Stop square only while busy with empty input; stop row names created tasks (e2e stop cases, server stop tests)
- [x] Tasks are created only when a reply lands, never on send (server test "send creates no todo")

## What

On xiechimon/cairn that meant intake would claim #1849, #1850 and #1851 (all `waits-ian`, "after the feature freeze") ahead of the unassigned #2006.

How: `apps/server/src/services/issue-intake.ts` adds `ISSUE_INTAKE_HOLD_LABELS` and checks it in the candidate loop next to the lane check from #2010 (both now read one lower-cased label list). The ADR 0021 D5 revision note from #2010 names the hold labels.

## Verified

## What

Recorded free costs and partial costs remain unchanged. Unknown null costs can be filled on a later startup after pricing becomes available.

This does not complete the historical data-repair goal from #1797. Old zero placeholders and recorded free usage have the same stored representation, so this PR preserves both. mergedPulls.title: server+eval(1920): route chief todos to the right project, add project-routing eval
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Answers #1920. When a team has several projects, the Chief has to put each todo in the right one.

`composeChiefSystemPrompt` in `apps/server/src/services/chief.ts` now lists each project with its `description` and `githubRepo`. Null fields are left out. The working rules gain one project-attribution bullet:
- Use the project the user names.
- Otherwise investigate first: compare descriptions, read files with `docs`, look at `todos`. Then pick one with evidence and say why in the reply.
- Call `ask_user` only when candidates stay tied, list only those candidates, and create no todo that turn.
- A request that touches several projects gets one todo per project, with the order written in the spec.
- A question with no change asked gets an answer and no todo.

New eval flow `project-routing` (`.claude/hillclimb/project-routing/`, `integration/eval/project-routing/`):
- Seeds `docs-site`, `digest-bot` and `bench` next to `eval-project`. Each has a description, set through `PATCH /api/projects/:id`, and a small hosted repo under `seeds/`.
- Has 13 cases: 2 named, 5 inferable, 2 tied, 2 cross-project, 2 question only.
- `gradeRoutingCase` grades on the projectId of the todos the turn left open. It does not read the transcript.
- The flow is registered in `scripts/eval-capabilities.json`, in the `docs/feature-map.md` coverage table, and in `scripts/ops/eval-weekly.sh`.

Changes to the shared eval code:
- `TurnEvidence.createdTodoRows` carries `projectId`.
- `seedRepoContent` takes a seed directory.
- `settleChiefTurn` cancels pending `ask_user` cards, so a turn that asks can finish without a user.
- `checkHarness` hashes a flow's declared `harness_paths` together with the chief-dispatch list.

## Verified

The new prompt test, run against the old `chief.ts` from origin/main, fails:

```
× systemPrompt lists each project with its description and carries the project-attribution rule (#1920)
AssertionError: expected '你是「总管」（Chief）…' to contain '"description":"官网 cairn.xmon.me 的静态站点"'
```

On this branch, the prompt test and the grader tests pass:

```
pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/chief-settings.test.ts integration/test/project-routing-grade.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
```

I also ran a negative control on the grader. With the name-boundary guards and the closed-todo filter removed from `grade.mts`, two tests fail: "a todo the chief closed in the same turn does not count" and "a project name inside a longer word does not count as naming that project".

`pnpm exec vitest run --changed` against origin/main gave 402 files, 5408 passed. `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm spec:parse` are green. `pnpm prepush` printed `[prepush] PASS (25 checks)`.

The real-model run of the new flow has not happened. A cloud session has no relay-186 key. The weekly omarchy run (`eval-weekly.sh`) records the first baseline after merge.

## Upstream

No equivalent exists. The flow reuses the chief-dispatch runner, stack and grading shape from memory-regression. It adds no new mechanism.

## Risk

Two-way door.
- The prompt change affects every Chief turn: one extra rule line, plus a description per project when one is set. The chief-settings tests cover it.
- Cancelling pending `ask_user` cards in `settleChiefTurn` also applies to chief-dispatch and memory-regression. Before this change, a turn there that called `ask_user` waited until the timeout and was recorded as a harness error.
- `checkHarness` now includes the paths declared in each flow's `_state.json`. That changes the memory-regression sha, so its next run needs `--approve-harness`, which the weekly script already passes.
- `chief.ts`, `stack.mts` and `integration/eval/**` are protected paths under ADR 0025/0026. This PR needs the independent review.

One self-review finding is not fixed. A clean answer for case `i01` needs the Chief to read the READMEs, and the grader cannot tell whether it read them or guessed. Only the final placement is scored.

## Acceptance

- [x] The prompt carries project descriptions and the attribution rule: `apps/server/test/chief-settings.test.ts` (#1920 test).
- [x] Eval family with named, inferable, tied, cross-project and question-only cases: `.claude/hillclimb/project-routing/cases.json`; the ledger tests in `integration/test/project-routing-grade.test.ts`.
- [x] Grader scores placement, ask and answer outcomes: the `gradeRoutingCase` tests, plus the negative control above.
- [x] The flow is registered for the weekly real-model run: `scripts/ops/eval-weekly.sh`, `scripts/eval-capabilities.json`.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What
Before: Vercel's Git integration created a deployment for every push to every PR branch. Most were cancelled by the ignore step or refused by the Hobby daily cap ("Deployment rate limited — retry in 24 hours"), and each left a Vercel status on the PR, often red. The `git.deploymentEnabled` main-only setting from #1814 did not stop PR deployments.

After: `site/vercel.json` turns Git deployments off, and a `site-deploy` workflow runs `vercel deploy --prod` only on pushes to main that change `site/`. The workflow is inert until the repo variable `VERCEL_DEPLOY` is `on` and the `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` secrets exist; the Vercel project's Git connection is removed separately so PRs get no Vercel status at all.

## Verified
Statuses checked on current PR heads: #1905 and #1889 show "Deployment rate limited", #1856 and #1857 show "Canceled by Ignored Build Step" — PR deployments still happen today.

mergedPulls.title: server(1791): plans that pass the contract check confirm themselves on non-human projects
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Before: a plan that reached `confirm` waited for a person unless the chief happened to be watching that todo. On 2026-10-25/26 this stranded #1671, #1612, #1617 and #1618 at `confirm` for hours, because they were dispatched or restarted outside the chief.

After: a plan that reaches `confirm` waits there for a grace window (`PLAN_AUTO_CONFIRM_GRACE_MS`, 10 minutes). Then the scheduler tick confirms it with actor `server` if all of these hold: the plan passes `checkPlanContract`, the project's merge policy is not `human`, the todo is not a split parent, the latest feedback is not a user plan revision, no chief question is pending on it, and the plan has no non-empty `Open questions` / `Decisions needed` / `Decision points` section. The chief keeps its window to ask the user or hold a plan with a real decision point (the first independent review blocked an immediate confirm for that reason), and a plan that names an open decision waits for a person. `confirm_builds` on an already-confirmed build is a no-op instead of a 409. Projects on `human` behave as before (ADR 0026).

Test fixtures: the shared project helpers in `apps/server/test/helpers.ts` and `integration/test/helpers.ts` now default to an explicit `human` policy, so tests of the confirm gate keep their meaning. The new test opts into `autonomous`. `token-auth.test.ts`'s env-mapping case no longer reads the real `~/.cairn/token` of the machine it runs on; it failed on any host that runs a token-protected Cairn, such as omarchy since 2026-10-26.

## Verified

`apps/server/test/plan-server-auto-confirm.test.ts` fails on main (the plan stays in `confirm`) and passes here. Its cases: a clean plan on an autonomous project confirms after the grace window and not before; a plan with open questions, a pending chief question, or a `human` project stays in `confirm`.

```
[prepush] PASS (21 checks)
```

## Upstream

No new mechanism; reuses the existing confirm path (extracted as `applyBuildConfirm`).

## Risk

Two-way door. A plan is held only if the chief asks, the plan names an open decision, or the project is `human`; otherwise it starts after ten minutes, as ADR 0026 intends. `chief-tools.ts` is touched (protected path), so the independent review applies.

## Acceptance

- [x] A plan reaching `confirm` on an autonomous project with no chief watch moves to `building` and leaves a gate announcement.
- [x] The same on a `human` project stays in `confirm`; split parents and revisions stay in `confirm`.

mergedPulls.title: daemon+server(1829): a hook-rejected closing push becomes a ci-fix round, and agent-opened PRs are recorded
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Before: on 2026-10-26 Cairn's build agent for #1618 opened PR #1812 itself, then the daemon's closing `git push` ran the repo's pre-push hook, the hook failed, and the build ended `failed` with `prNumber = null`. ci-loop only watches builds with a recorded PR, so the red `pr-evidence` check on #1812 was never picked up and nothing fixed it.

After: a closing push rejected by a local hook no longer fails the build. The daemon reports the hook output (`pushHookOutput` on the done body) and the server queues a same-branch `[ci-fix]` step carrying it, under the shared ci-fix round cap. After a build step the server looks up an open PR whose head is the build branch and records `prNumber` / `prUrl` on the build, so ci-loop and the merge gate see PRs the agent opened itself.

## Verified

Tests written first and red on main: `apps/server/test/ci-loop.test.ts` (hook rejection queues a `[ci-fix]` with the hook output; an agent-opened PR is recorded and picked up), `apps/daemon/test/runner-delivery.test.ts`, `apps/daemon/test/git.test.ts`.

```
[prepush] PASS (21 checks)
packages/shared/test/snapshot.test.ts: machineDoneBody snapshot updated for pushHookOutput
```

## Upstream

Reuses the existing `[ci-fix]` prompt, round counter and dead-loop message from `ci-loop.ts`.

## Risk

Two-way door. Adds an optional `pushHookOutput` field to the machine done body; older daemons omit it. Touches the machine finish path (`machine-finish-step.ts`, protected category ⑤), so the independent review applies.

## Acceptance

- [x] A build whose push is rejected by a pre-push hook gets a `[ci-fix]` step carrying the hook output instead of `failed`.

mergedPulls.title: scripts: docs-only prepush runs the tests that read the changed docs
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU?thread=cmsg_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdUSDzifPSdf5aZ6ZivW1FXws)_

## What

A docs-only push now runs the tests that read the changed docs. `scripts/doc-reader-tests.mjs` takes the changed paths, finds `*.test.ts` and `*.test.mjs` files that name each path (`git grep -F`), and runs them with `node --test` and `pnpm exec vitest run`. Only docs under a directory are matched, because root-level names such as `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` appear in many tests as fixture file names; `integration/` suites (they boot a real server) and files in `scripts/prepush-known-red.json` are skipped, and `git grep` runs with `color.ui=never`. `scripts/prepush.mjs` runs the step for the docs in any local push, docs-only or mixed; the CI plan is unchanged because CI runs the full suites. `scripts/doc-reader-tests.test.mjs` covers the selection and is added to the prepush self-tests and the CI self-test step.

This came from the English cleanup: #1765 translated `docs/ops/agent-bot-identity.md`, the docs-only prepush ran only the language gate, and CI then went red on `apps/server/test/codeowners.test.ts`, which matches a sentence in that doc.

## Verified

Negative control, the real #1765 mistake: the translated `docs/ops/agent-bot-identity.md` on top of main, with the test still matching the old Chinese sentence.

```
$ node scripts/doc-reader-tests.mjs docs/ops/agent-bot-identity.md
[doc-reader-tests] pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/codeowners.test.ts
 FAIL  |@xiechimon/cairn| test/codeowners.test.ts > docs/ops/agent-bot-identity.md > states that Code Owners review turns on only after the bot pushes the PR
      Tests  1 failed | 7 passed (8)
exit=1
```

Same command on main's doc:

```
      Tests  8 passed (8)
exit=0
$ node --test scripts/doc-reader-tests.test.mjs scripts/prepush.test.mjs
ℹ pass 16
ℹ fail 0
$ git push   # pre-push hook
[prepush] PASS (22 checks)
```

## Upstream

No equivalent: `scripts/prepush-vitest.mjs` runs `vitest --changed`, which follows imports, and a test that reads a Markdown file with `readFileSync` does not import it.

## Risk

Two-way door. Blast radius: local pushes that change a doc under a directory run the unit tests that name it; root-level docs and docs no test names add nothing. `node scripts/doc-reader-tests.mjs README.md AGENTS.md` selects no tests. CI is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- [x] A docs-only push runs the tests that name the changed doc (Verified negative control)
- [x] The CI plan for docs-only changes is unchanged (`prepushPlan(['docs/lessons.md'], 'ci')` in `scripts/prepush.test.mjs`)

_Requested by **ian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU?thread=cmsg_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdUGqo6tCR3PXY8Nw5ZQB2Dsv)_

## What

`/app` used to open the four-column board, which repeats the same cards a person has to scan for what needs them. The landing page is now a home in three sections, and the board moves behind its own sidebar entry.

- New `apps/web/src/board/home.tsx`: `HomeSections` renders `需要你` (pending column, week-old ones folded as in #1807), `在跑` (building column, with not-started tasks folded below it, each with a start action that shows orchestration state) and `做完了` (done in the last 7 days, five shown, a link to the board). Sections read `COLUMNS` and `sortColumnTodos`, so home and the board cannot disagree on which card goes where. The inbox rows from #1807 moved here and share `TaskRow` / `RowAction`.
- `view=board` opens the board. The sidebar shows `工作台` (home, carries the needs-you badge) and `看板` (board); the old `需要我处理` row is gone since home leads with that list. The page title follows the view, and links off the board drop `view=board`.
- Filters keep the current view; a filter that matches nothing shows the existing filter-empty state on home too.
- `boot-skeleton.js` draws a centered row list unless the URL asks for the board, and the boot shape cache records only the board.
- E2E specs that test the board now open `view=board`.

![home, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/e26f8401/docs/verify/home-inbox/home-light.png)
![home with not-started open, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/e26f8401/docs/verify/home-inbox/home-dark.png)
![board view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/e26f8401/docs/verify/home-inbox/kanban-light.png)
![phone, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/e26f8401/docs/verify/home-inbox/phone-home-light.png)
![phone, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/e26f8401/docs/verify/home-inbox/phone-home-dark.png)

## Verified

The affected e2e set first, then the failing specs after the fixes, then the full suite through `pnpm prepush` on push.

```
e2e:affected (falls back to full on shared surfaces): first run 57 failed, all specs that opened /app expecting the board
after adding view=board and the review fixes: failing set + board-shell/paper-sidebar/dead-buttons rerun: 219 passed, 2 failed under load, both pass on rerun (36 passed)
pnpm prepush full e2e, first push: 7 failed (topbar title and schedules link kept view=board; the new sidebar-focus-ring spec named the old sidebar rows); dead i18n key 需要我处理 caught by the liveness test
after the fixes, pnpm prepush full e2e: 1298 passed (12.6m)
new e2e: home splits work into three sections; project filter keeps home; filter-empty on home; 390px home clears the new-task bar
pnpm lint / typecheck / spec:parse / ui-drift / single-use-helper / comment / english gates: pass
```

## Upstream

No new mechanism. Rows reuse `ATTENTION`, `cardFace`, `COLUMNS`, `sortColumnTodos`, `splitStale`, `relativeTime`, `SpiralMark`, `Button` and `Skeleton`.

## Risk

Two-way door, web only. Blast radius: every link to `/app` now lands on home; deep links to the board need `view=board`. Bookmarks to `?column=pending` still open the inbox. In fixture mode the not-started start action does nothing, the same as the board card's start link today. Once #1800 ships the server needs-you query, `需要你` should switch to it. A site-wide redesign will rework the home layout next (running and recently merged first, needs-you only for exceptions); this PR gives it the route and component split to build on.

## Acceptance

- [x] `/app` shows `需要你` / `在跑` / `做完了`, no board columns (e2e)
- [x] Sidebar `看板` opens the board and `工作台` comes back, badge stays on `工作台` (e2e)
- [x] Project or tag filters keep the view; zero matches show the filter-empty state (e2e)
- [x] Phone: home scrolls as one page and the last row clears the new-task bar (390px e2e, screenshots)

## Issues

Follows #1807. Unrelated to #1800.

mergedPulls.title: web: keep sidebar focus rings whole and hide them after a mouse click plus Escape
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU?thread=cmsg_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU1BDWjZ6swtDzF1uNSgHeiV)_

## What

Clicking the `工作台` sidebar row and then pressing Escape painted a dark green ring under the row, with its top and sides cut off. Two causes:

1. Chromium counts Escape as keyboard interaction, so a row focused by a mouse click starts matching `:focus-visible`.
2. The sidebar `nav` scrolls (`overflow-y-auto`). Rows sit flush with its edges, so the global ring (2px, offset 2px) is clipped on the left, right and top.

Changes:

- `apps/web/src/pointer-focus.ts` sets `html[data-pointer-focus]` on `pointerdown` and clears it on any keydown except Escape and bare modifiers. `apps/web/src/styles/app.css` hides the ring on non-text controls while it is set. `main.tsx` installs it at boot. Tab and Shift+Tab still show the ring, and Escape after Tab keeps it.
- `apps/web/src/lib/focus-ring.ts` adds `FOCUS_RING_INSET` (2px ring, offset -2px). Sidebar rows (`ROW`) and rail rows (`RAIL_ROW`) in `board/sidebar.tsx` use it, so the ring follows the row radius and stays inside the scroller.
- `FadeScrollerViewport` (transcript and chief drawer) uses the same inset ring. It showed the browser default `auto` ring, which its panel clipped on all four sides.

A site sweep (Tab through 12 pages plus the collapsed rail, checking every focused element's ring against each overflow ancestor) found only these three places. After the fix the sweep finds none.

![before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/0ae50397/docs/verify/sidebar-focus-ring/before-after.png)

## Verified

New spec `apps/web/e2e/sidebar-focus-ring.spec.ts` (6 cases), run on the old code. All 6 failed, for example:

```
mouse click then Escape on a sidebar row paints no focus ring
-   "clippedBy": Array [],
+   "clippedBy": Array [ "nav:left+right+top" ],
-   "outline": "none",
+   "outline": "solid 2px",
transcript scroller focus ring stays inside its panel
-   "outline": "solid 2px",
+   "outline": "auto 1px",
```

The same spec on this branch:

```
6 passed (5.8s)
```

Related e2e on this branch (registry-focus-ring, sidebar-*, overlay-focus, search-focus, escape-*, cds-sidebar, paper-sidebar, chief-*, transcript-*):

```
173 passed (1.6m)
```

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the comment discipline gate and `pnpm prepush` pass.

## Upstream

Base UI and the registry components have no input-modality tracking. React Aria's `useFocusVisible` is not a dependency, and it treats Escape as keyboard input too, so it would not fix case 1. The tracker is 20 lines with no dependency.

## Risk

Two-way door, CSS and one document listener. While the pointer flag is set, the ring is hidden on buttons, links, tabs, checkboxes, switches and `[tabindex]` elements that are not text fields. Text inputs keep their ring. Any non-Escape key clears the flag. The full e2e suite runs in CI. code-review (low) flagged the duplicated ring class, now shared through `lib/focus-ring.ts`. It also asked whether the new CSS rule sits in the base layer. It sits in `@layer utilities`, and the two Escape cases in the new spec prove it overrides the row utilities.

## Acceptance

- [x] Mouse click then Escape on a sidebar or rail row shows no ring (spec cases 1 and 2)
- [x] Keyboard focus ring on sidebar and rail rows follows the row radius and is not clipped (cases 3 and 4)
- [x] Escape after Tab keeps the ring for keyboard users (case 5)
- [x] Site sweep for the same clipping, transcript scroller fixed (case 6)
- [x] Before and after screenshots in light and dark (image above)

## Issues

Reported in the project thread, no ticket.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU?thread=cmsg_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdUTmSCbGPkshsfGAWJkdTeJq)_

## What

The `⌘↵` hint inside the new-task start button was unreadable while the button was disabled (empty draft). `DIALOG_PRIMARY_BUTTON` paints the disabled button `secondary`, but the `Kbd` kept `text-primary-foreground/80`, so cream ink sat on a cream fill: 1.08:1 light, 1.25:1 dark. The hint now uses `bg-current/10 text-current` in `apps/web/src/overlay/new-task-dialog.tsx` and follows the button ink in both states.

The same sweep fixed:

- `DIALOG_TEXT_BUTTON` (`components/ui/dialog-shell.tsx`): disabled text button was opacity 50% (2.21:1 light). It now keeps full opacity with `text-content-tertiary`.
- Active sidebar project count (`board/sidebar.tsx`): `content-tertiary` on the active row tint was 4.18:1. The active row uses `content-secondary`.
- `[data-slot="kbd"]` hides under `@media (pointer: coarse)` in `styles/app.css`; touch users have no keyboard, and `kbd.tsx` stays pristine shadcn.
- The empty todo column ghost card no longer repeats the `C` hint shown on the board new-task bar.
- The card branch button (20px) gets a 24px hit area through an `after` pseudo-element; row height unchanged.

The gate: axe exempts disabled controls and `aria-hidden` kbd hints from `color-contrast`, which is why `a11y-axe.spec.ts` stayed green. `apps/web/e2e/contrast-probe.ts` walks every text node, kbd hint, disabled control (3:1 floor) and native `::placeholder`, composes the real backdrop and opacity, and reports anything under WCAG AA. Each `a11y-axe` test now runs it after axe, and a filled new-task dialog page joins the list.

![desktop before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/60192f20c0e39875acfeec30d73cd8f6197907bf/docs/verify/contrast-hints/desktop-before-after.png)
![phone before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/60192f20c0e39875acfeec30d73cd8f6197907bf/docs/verify/contrast-hints/phone-before-after.png)

## Verified

Old build (`origin/main` fixture dist) with the new spec:

```
E2E_PORT=8396 pnpm exec playwright test e2e/a11y-axe.spec.ts
    Error: low contrast outside axe on new task dialog (light)
      kind: disabled, ratio: 2.21, text: `保存`
      kind: kbd, ratio: 1.08, text: ⌘↵
    Error: low contrast outside axe on project tasks (light)
      kind: text, ratio: 4.18, text: 1
    Error: low contrast outside axe on new task dialog (dark)
      kind: disabled, ratio: 2.94, text: `保存`
      kind: kbd, ratio: 1.25, text: ⌘↵
  3 failed
  43 passed (33.8s)
```

This branch:

```
E2E_PORT=8397 pnpm exec playwright test e2e/a11y-axe.spec.ts

axe-core is already the contrast check here, and by WCAG rule it skips disabled controls and hidden kbd hints, so it cannot catch this bug. The probe runs inside the existing axe spec after axe, checking the same text plus the nodes axe exempts. It is not a second runner.

Two-way door. The visual change is limited to the disabled dialog text button, the start button hint, one sidebar count tone, touch-only kbd visibility, one removed hint and one wider hit area. mergedPulls.title: server(1753): default to autonomous merges with independent review
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Before: projects defaulted to `mergePolicy = human`, and any protected path or deleted test blocked the merge-readiness gate as `protected-path` / `test-deleted`, both of class `human`. The chief prompt told the chief that merges are human-only.

After (ADR 0026, #1754): projects default to `autonomous`. Protected paths and deleted tests add `independent-review-missing` until a review verdict exists that is bound to the current `headSha` and `patchDigest`, comes from a reviewer other than the author running on a different model, and answers `gateLoosening` and `evalRulerChange`; if either answer is true the gate blocks with `review-blocking`. Projects that explicitly choose `human` keep the old behaviour. The chief prompt and spec 28 (P8-1 shadow phase, D7) now point at ADR 0026.

## Verified

Tests were written first and failed on main. Evidence is in `docs/verify/1753/`.

```
merge-gate-readiness, chief-auto-confirm and the other touched suites: green (490 tests in the worker run; 204 + 8 re-run after rebase)
pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck: clean
[prepush] PASS (20 checks)
```

Two tests that arrived from main during the rebase (#1643's docs-only cases) asserted the old `protected-path` / `test-deleted` codes; they now assert `independent-review-missing`.

## Upstream

No new mechanism; extends the existing D3 verdict binding with reviewer identity, model and the two mandatory answers.

## Risk

Fails closed: if a caller does not pass the author's id and model, no verdict can count as independent and protected changes stay blocked. Not in this PR, tracked as follow-ups: the npm release workflow without a human step, and the weekly sample of merged autonomous PRs.

## Acceptance

- [x] A new project reads `autonomous`.
- [x] A protected-path PR without a bound independent verdict is blocked with `independent-review-missing`; with one it is ready; a verdict reporting gate loosening blocks.
- [x] The chief prompt no longer claims merges are human-only.
- [x] spec 28 rows point at ADR 0026.

mergedPulls.title: docs(1753): ADR 0026 machine trust replaces the human merge gates
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Before: ADR 0021 and spec 28 kept a person before every merge that was not plain product code: `mergePolicy` defaulted to `human`, protected paths forced `human`, a ten-PR shadow phase was required before `autonomous`, ADRs and specs were merged by the user, and npm publishing always needed a human. The running system had already moved past that (code-owner review off, an independent review agent plus GitHub auto-merge), so the written rules and reality disagreed.

After: ADR 0026 records ian's decision of 2026-10-26 (option A, following poteto's practice): `autonomous` by default; protected paths need CI green plus an independent review verdict bound to the exact patch, from a different model than the author's, that also answers "does this loosen a gate" and "does this change the eval ruler"; no shadow phase; ADRs merge through the same review; npm publishing is automatic; a weekly post-hoc sample of merged PRs goes to ian and any miss becomes a correction issue. ADR 0021's machine checks (D2 sha-bound merge, D3 patch-bound verdicts, D5 issue text as data, D6 rollback) stay.

## Verified

Docs-only change. `node scripts/english-only-gate.mjs` reports 0 lines with Chinese text; pre-push checks passed on push.

## Upstream

No new mechanism in this PR. Implementation follows in #1753.

## Risk

One-way in spirit: it removes the human before the merge. Mitigated by the emergency stop, the daily cap, the circuit breaker with revert PRs, and the weekly sample, all kept from ADR 0021 and spec 28.

After: when a build step ends abnormally and its branch has commits ahead of the base, the daemon pushes the branch and sends the commit list; the fallback report lists them and the changes API shows the files. Restarting that build continues on the pushed branch (the same rework path builds with a PR already use). The build-step duration budget now resets on progress, so a step that keeps working is not cut at one hour; `CAIRN_STREAM_DURATION_CAP_MS` stays an absolute override.

## Verified

Tests were written first and failed on main: `integration/test/build-failure-preservation.test.ts` (pushed ref, both commit hashes in the fallback report, changes API files, restart reuses the build) and new cases in `apps/daemon/test/runner-stream-timeout.test.ts` (progress resets the budget, the env override stays absolute).

```
100 selected tests: passed
pnpm lint: no errors
pnpm typecheck: all packages done
packages/shared/test/snapshot.test.ts: machineDoneBody snapshot updated for preservedCommits, 80 passed
[prepush] PASS (20 checks)
```

## Upstream

No new mechanism. Reuses the existing rework path in `applyBuildStepAction` restart and the existing fallback report.

## Risk

Two-way door. Adds an optional `preservedCommits` field to the machine done body (older daemons simply omit it). Touches `machines.ts` (protected path, so the independent review applies).

## Acceptance

- [x] A build step that commits and then hits the duration cap leaves the branch pushed, and the fallback report lists the commits.
- [x] Restart after that failure enqueues the next step on the same branch, with the earlier commits present.

mergedPulls.title: server(1732): confirm-gate wake carries the plan and the conversation tool has a budget
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Before: at the confirm gate the chief was told to read the plan with the `conversation` tool, which returned the whole planner session with no limit. On 2026-10-25 (Cairn trial run of #1671, todo #89) that put 319,873 tokens into one chief call, the provider rejected it, nothing retried, and the todo sat in `confirm` for an hour until a person confirmed it.

After: the confirm-gate wake carries the latest plan version of the build, capped at 40,000 characters; a missing or truncated plan tells the chief not to auto-confirm. The `conversation` tool returns newest messages first within a 60,000-character budget, marks `truncated`, pages with a `before` message id, and summarises tool calls by name instead of dumping arguments and results. A chief turn that fails on a gate wake is retried once in a fresh session; a second failure leaves a system line on the build asking for a person.

mergedPulls.title: web: claude-style shell, needs-you strip and calmer chief launcher
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

The board and the app shell now follow the claude.ai layout, and the board opens on what needs you. The direction came from a user-feedback study of AI coding-agent orchestrators (Vibe Kanban, Multica, Cline Kanban, Claude Code desktop, Codex, Cursor agents, Devin, Jules, Agent HQ, Linear agents). Users praised boards that show at a glance what is running and what waits on them, and complained most when status was faint or when acting on something meant leaving the overview. ian approved the prototype.

Shell (`pages/shell.tsx`, `board/sidebar.tsx`): `SHEET_PANEL` is edge-to-edge, with no inset margin, rounded corners or `::after` ring. It keeps `isolate`. The sidebar keeps `--surface-1` behind a 1px right hairline. Rows are 36px with 1.5px icon strokes. The active row is a flat `--hover-1` fill instead of a white card. The `新任务` row is a filled `--card-button` plus disc without the `C` badge; the shortcut stays.

Board header (`board/board.tsx`): the top bar loses its rule and its `新任务` button. A centered one-line `board-new-task-bar` with the spiral mark opens the existing new-task surface. `NeedsYouStrip` lists the pending column (`viewTodos('pending')`) with each card's attention action. It follows the card's orchestration lock (`编排中`, no action while the chief owns the todo), shows `打开`, and links `查看全部` through `withColumnParam` so filters survive. A `上次查看后` line counts done and failed transitions in the filtered list between the stored `cairn.board.lastSeenAt` and this visit.

Phone (`styles/app.css`, up to 640px): one stacked list, empty columns hidden, `.board-main` scrolls as one page so the strip scrolls away. The new-task bar is pinned at the bottom. On the board only, the chief launcher and the window's zoom origin move above it.

Motion and status: the chief window grows out of the launcher (`--dur-window` 320ms, `--ease-drawer`, scale .4 from the launcher centre). Running cards show the spinning spiral (`SpiralMark` from `chief-fab-icon.tsx`) instead of the breathing bot; the dead `card-breath` keyframes and `--animate-breath` are gone. The chief launcher sits on `bg-card` with body ink and `--fab-shadow` instead of the dark green disc; `--fab-badge*` are removed.

Fix found on the way: `toggleTag` / `toggleProject` in `routes/board-page.tsx` built the next filter from render-time state, so a second pick before the re-render dropped the first. This is the `board-filter` e2e "flake" seen on three pre-push runs. Both now read the current URL.

`DESIGN.md`: new "Current shell and board surface" section, chief launcher paragraph, and the motion section translated to English with the new rows.

![board dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/cairn/a3b4f5070e19fca762c37d137f7c19dd351705d4/docs/verify/claude-shell/board-dark.jpg)

mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What
`pnpm traj:push` now keeps a local record of the traces it has pushed, keyed by endpoint and trace, under the Cairn data directory rather than in the repo. Re-pushing skips them and reports `skipped_already_pushed=N`. `--force` pushes them again. A different endpoint is a separate target and pushes normally, while a changed auth header does not count as a new target. If a push fails partway, a retry skips the parts that already succeeded. Background: on 2026-10-25 a real push to omarchy's Langfuse (v4, events_only mode) showed that re-pushing identical trace and span ids stores new rows (12 rows for 6 ids), so the ticket's 「重推一次条数不变」 needed this. The decision is recorded on #1570.

## Verified
- The 6 new CLI tests went red against the old implementation. They run against a local fake OTLP receiver: the second push sends 0 requests and reports `skipped_already_pushed=2`; only a newly added build is pushed; `--force` re-sends all 8 spans and a later push is skipped again; a different endpoint pushes; a changed key doesn't re-push; a retry after a partial failure skips what already succeeded. `trajectory-push.test.ts` passes (20 tests).
- `typecheck`, `lint`, `prepush-vitest`; single-use-helper and comment gates at 0; prepush on push.

## Upstream
OTLP/HTTP; Langfuse v4 events_only does not dedupe by span id.

## Risk
Deleting the local record file means everything gets pushed again. That's the same as `--force`.

## Acceptance
- [x] Re-pushing the same pack adds no rows: the second push sends nothing (CLI test).
- [x] `--force` pushes again, and a new endpoint is pushed normally (CLI tests).

## What

First step of #1481. A team image could reach a task an outside author wrote: an attachment token line copied from a public self-issue into a new issue survived `importGithubIssue`, and `machineAttachmentDownload` served attachments by the machine's team while ignoring the token's team segment.

mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What
`pnpm traj:push <packs.jsonl>` reads `traj:export` output and POSTs it as OTLP/HTTP JSON to `CAIRN_OTEL_ENDPOINT` (with `CAIRN_OTEL_HEADERS`). It doesn't use the Langfuse or OTel SDK, so the lockfile doesn't change. Each build becomes a trace with root span `invoke_agent`, one child span per step, `chat` spans for model turns and `execute_tool` spans for tool calls. Fields follow the OTel GenAI conventions, and everything outside them goes under `cairn.*`. Trace and span ids come from sha256 of buildId/stepId/turn, so pushing the same pack twice sends byte-identical bodies. The whole request goes through `redactSecrets` before sending. Every GenAI field name lives in `genai-conventions.ts`, and a test fails if `gen_ai.` appears in any other source file.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian**_

## What

Research for #1607: can ACP (Agent Client Protocol) serve as one execution surface for outside agent CLIs, instead of one hand-written bridge per agent? The result is `docs/research/1607-acp-execution-surface.md`.

Conclusions in the doc:

- Build an ACP backend, but keep the existing `pi.ts` and `claude-code.ts` bridges. ACP fits a third family: agent CLIs installed on the machine that hold their own login.
- Start with Gemini CLI. Its binary ships `--acp` (registry `@google/gemini-cli@0.65.0`, released 2026-10-20), and the TypeScript SDK docs use it as the reference agent.
- Codex and Claude Code reach ACP through adapters, not their own ACP server. The Claude SDK bridge already carries usage, skill denial and strict MCP that an adapter would drop.
- Copilot CLI (`--acp`, still public preview on its agents page) and Hermes (`hermes acp`, `v0.22.5`, not in the auth registry) wait until the Gemini probe is green.
- A trajectory pack (#1511) cannot be rebuilt from ACP events alone: four-way token counts, cache writes, the five cost parts, plan versions, gate verdicts and merge results are not in the stable protocol.

The doc compares each capability the two current bridges provide (streaming, tool call records, stopReason and usage, resume, cancel, command-gate, MCP injection, skills injection) with ACP coverage, sketches `apps/daemon/src/backend/acp.ts`, covers spec 17, ADR 0018 and ADR 0020, and ends with two build ticket drafts. mergedPulls.title: server(1403): CI grind reads checks by head SHA, only required checks decide, BEHIND and DIRTY handled
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 3 of #1403, the last segment of bootstrap phase P2 (`docs/spec/28` §4 P2). It makes the CI grind read GitHub the way GitHub itself decides mergeability. The plan, GitHub facts and failure modes are in [seg3-plan.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/52f5ffaeff20f24d9ac8cc583a7a57bf4e791f9a/docs/verify/1403/seg3-plan.md).

All in `apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts` unless noted.

**Checks by head SHA.** For the build's own open PR targeting the default branch (`isOwnOpenDefaultPull`, `lib/github.ts`), the grind reads `pulls/{n}` and then the check runs of that head SHA. Any other PR is read by branch name, without conflict handling.

**Push lag.** Within 5 minutes after pacman pushed, a PR whose head is not that push is not judged. Steps that pushed nothing do not count as a push. Past the grace, the PR head decides.

**Only required checks decide green.** The required list (`githubRequiredChecks`, `lib/github.ts`) combines classic branch protection (ignored when `enforcement_level` is `off`) and ruleset checks, and keeps `/` in branch names. It is cached 10 minutes, and a failed read is not retried by other cards in the same sweep. Runs that share a name pass on one success.

**Blocked instead of green or fixed**, each with one hint per round:
- cancelled, neutral or skipped on a required check;
- `action_required`, which is not sent to a `[ci-fix]` round;
- a required check still missing after the grace.

**BEHIND** gets a hint naming update-branch with `expected_head_sha`. No request is sent.

**DIRTY** gets a same-branch `[merge-conflict]` build step that merges the default branch in, with no rebase or force-push. The branch name is shell-quoted in the prompt. At most 2 rounds: at building the card then goes to failed, at review it gets a hint. A round stops unclaimed verify and review steps; at review the card first goes back to queued, and verify is queued again once it is back in review.

**`step.finishedAt`** (`apps/server/src/db/schema.ts`, migration `0047_step_finished_at.sql`) is written when a build step stops and orders the last pushed checkpoint (`builds.ts`).

**From the last pr-gate on #1509:** the closing-shape check on the squash title now tests the PR title alone. With " (#n)" appended, titles such as "Add CI fix" matched and lost their title.

**Docs:** spec 02's GitHub bullet; spec 28 §8 changes only the P2 row.

## Verified

Failure modes first, in the plan (§8, §10, §12 to §15, §18). GitHub's REST facts for pulls, check runs, branch protection, rules for a branch and update-branch are quoted there with their doc URLs.

Tests first ([seg3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/52f5ffaeff20f24d9ac8cc583a7a57bf4e791f9a/docs/verify/1403/seg3-red-green.txt)), `pr-seg3.test.ts` and the touched suites. Each red leg ran before its fix and went green after:

```
plan        26 failed | 13 passed
review 1    11 failed | 40 passed
review 2     6 failed | 54 passed
review 3     5 failed | 61 passed
review 4     5 failed | 67 passed
review 5     4 failed | 72 passed
merge review 3 failed | 76 passed
title fix    3 failed | 10 passed
```

Mutations ([seg3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/52f5ffaeff20f24d9ac8cc583a7a57bf4e791f9a/docs/verify/1403/seg3-mutations.txt)): 54 of 54 killed (23 base, then 9, 6, 7, 5, 3 and 1 for the later fixes). The first run's report misread vitest's summary; the file records that and the two test changes it led to.

Gates on `cde42fc` ([gates-seg3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/52f5ffaeff20f24d9ac8cc583a7a57bf4e791f9a/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg3.txt), three dated runs), all exit 0:
- lint, typecheck, spec:parse;
- `vitest run --changed origin/main` (155 files, 2150 passed);
- `e2e:affected` (8 passed; only server files differ from main now, so the server family ran).

The full server suite on the merge of main `d4fd908` passes 2459 tests. `db:check` passes with the migration at main's tail.

Reviews ([seg3-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/52f5ffaeff20f24d9ac8cc583a7a57bf4e791f9a/docs/verify/1403/seg3-reviews.txt)):
- /code-review at medium six times: five rounds on the segment, one on the merges of 2b. Each finding was fixed tests first or declined with a reason in the plan.
- /simplify, one pass.
- /security-review not needed: no file on the AGENTS.md list is touched.

## Upstream

No dependency. GitHub REST: `GET pulls/{n}`, `GET commits/{ref}/check-runs`, `GET branches/{branch}` (its protection summary) and `GET rules/branches/{branch}`, as quoted in the plan.

## Risk

Two decisions to confirm:
- Required checks that end `neutral` or `skipped` count as not passing, as the ticket's scope says. GitHub's own merge box accepts them, so a required job that a path filter skips leaves the card in building, with a hint each round.
- The rules endpoint's 403 counts as "no rulesets" only when its message is GitHub's plan wording (`/upgrade to github|enable this feature/i`). The docs list only 200 for this endpoint, so that wording is assumed. If GitHub words it differently, the card stays in building rather than being judged on a partial list.

Kept:
- A development or verify database that applied this branch's earlier migration numbers (0045 or 0046) before the renumber needs a reset; only databases that ran this unmerged branch are affected.
- A PR read that keeps failing leaves the card in building.
- The anonymous grind now makes more reads, against GitHub's hourly limit for unauthenticated requests.
- Commit-status-only required contexts become a hint after the grace, not green.
- The chief step's done or failed write has no `finishedAt`; `services/machines.ts` is on the security list, so the schema comment is narrowed to build steps instead.

From the pr-gate run at `52f5ffa` (go, no blocking finding), handed to pacman's own build as follow-ups:
- Without a GitHub connection the grind now reads the PR and the required list as well as the check runs, roughly 130 anonymous requests an hour for one building card against GitHub's 60. Once the shared per-IP budget is spent, the review reconcile and the #931 / #1217 guards skip for the rest of the hour.
- A required check that reports only as a commit status, or ends neutral or skipped, keeps the card in building with a hint each round and no automatic way out (the decision above).
- A `[merge-conflict]` round that finds nothing to commit (the conflict was resolved on GitHub first, or `dirty` was stale) fails at the zero-change artifact gate, as `[ci-fix]` rounds already do.
- With no required list, neutral and skipped runs do not block; the ticket's "neutral / skipped not green" applies to required checks only.
- Two spec 02 sentences still describe the old behaviour (the reconcile bullet's "no finish-time column", and the closing-shape clause after the title rule); they are corrected in the section 8 ledger PR that follows this one.

Handed to follow-up from the #1509 pr-gate (recorded in the reviews file): closing keywords in a PR description, a pending verify step claimed during the merge request, the ADR 0021 D2 note waiting for the user, a #1217 guard test with GitHub connected, and the unauthenticated merge route.

Live legs 待宿主: a real PR's required checks, BEHIND and DIRTY on GitHub.

This PR adds a migration. The user authorised the session on 2026-10-22 to merge once pr-gate is go and CI is green.

## Acceptance

- [x] Checks are read by the PR's head SHA, with push lag; only required checks decide green (`pr-seg3.test.ts`, red/green)
- [x] BEHIND hints update-branch; DIRTY queues a same-branch merge-conflict step, at most 2 rounds (`pr-seg3.test.ts`)
- [x] `step.finishedAt` written and used to order the last pushed checkpoint; migration 0047 at main's tail, `db:check` passes

mergedPulls.title: server(1403): pressing merge on a GitHub task merges its PR through the API
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 2b of #1403, bootstrap phase P2. It builds design D, which the user chose on 2026-10-22 ([decision](https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1403#issuecomment-6338182522)).

For a GitHub-form task whose build has a recorded PR, pressing merge in pacman now merges the PR through GitHub's REST API with `sha`. No machine merge step is queued for it. This also settles the earlier "option B" decision on #1414: the completion row is written only when the PR is actually merged.

**Routing (`apps/server/src/services/builds.ts`).** `requestMerge` sends a GitHub-form build with a recorded PR to `mergeThroughGithub`; `githubPrOf` is the single test for that. Everything else keeps today's merge step: hosted, local, and GitHub form without a PR. The wire answer stays `202 {delegated: true}`.

**Checks before the PUT, all without writes.**
1. The phase is review, or failed and restorable.
2. The build is the todo's current build, with no step in flight.
3. The #1217 guard passes, then the phase is checked again.
4. The permission gate passes.
5. There is a usable token:
   - no connection: 409 asking to connect GitHub;
   - token that does not decrypt: reconnect;
   - no secret box: server key.
6. No merge of this build is already in flight.

Then the server reads the PR and requires:
- it is the build's own PR, and its author has write access;
- its base is the default branch;
- its head equals the build's last pushed checkpoint (40 hex characters).

**The merge.** `PUT pulls/{n}/merge` (`githubMergePull` in `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`) with:
- `sha` = that checkpoint;
- `merge_method` squash;
- `commit_title` = `<PR title> (#n)`, or pacman's own `Merge pull request #n` when that text contains a closing keyword followed by a token with a digit;
- `commit_message` is always sent: `closes #N` only when the task came from an issue of the same repository, otherwise `Merged by pacman.`, so GitHub never fills the body from the PR.

| GitHub's answer | What pacman does |
|---|---|
| Merged | Announcement, a merged row, the card goes to done. |
| Refused (4xx), including a rate-limited 429 or 403 | 409 with GitHub's cleaned message, plus the wait time when known (`retry-after` first) and the next step. Nothing is written, and a failed card stays failed. |
| No clear answer (timeout, network error, 5xx, unreadable 200) | 202 and one row. Segment 1's merged read finishes the card on the next sweep. |

**Support around the merge.**
- An in-memory set of merges in flight feeds `hasActiveStep`, so the reconcile sweep never writes during the PUT.
- `lastPushedCheckpoint` is shared with the reconcile.
- The merge step's done tail no longer finishes a GitHub-form build that has a PR. This covers merge steps queued before the upgrade.
- Rate-limit headers have one parser (`rateLimitOf`) for the intake, the webhook and the merge. A value that is empty, negative, fractional or longer than ten digits counts as absent.

**From the post-merge pr-gate run on #1489.** Adopting another PR from the build's branch now requires the author's `author_association` to be OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, captured live. Also:
- the confirm-phase 409 is stated in spec 02;
- the foreign path's phase re-read is pinned;
- the `listFailures` cleanup is pinned;
- the skipped-relist stamp is pinned.

**Web.** The merge dialog shows the refusal text (en and zh), on the board and on the task detail page.

**Docs.**
- spec 02, A6 and §4.2, describe the new path.
- spec 28 §8 updates only the P2 row.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([seg2b-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a281674660f311387ef68b782912cae4c99987c5/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-failure-modes.txt)). They quote GitHub's merge endpoint parameters, status codes and response schema, the rate-limit rules, and the `author_association` enum. Dated notes were appended for the rate-limit change. The live capture of the branch PR list with author associations is [live-branch-pulls-assoc.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a281674660f311387ef68b782912cae4c99987c5/docs/verify/1403/live-branch-pulls-assoc.json).

Tests before code ([seg2b-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a281674660f311387ef68b782912cae4c99987c5/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-red-green.txt)). The final red leg runs the head's tests against main's sources:

```
red   Tests  88 failed | 187 passed (275)
green Tests  275 passed (275)
```

The rate-limit change and its review fix went red with 5 and then 4 failing tests before each fix. One case, an oversized header, was written together with its fix, and the file says so. The full server suite passes: 126 files, 2082 passed, 1 skipped.

Mutations ([seg2b-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a281674660f311387ef68b782912cae4c99987c5/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-mutations.txt)): 51 of 51 caught, plus 7 of 7 on the rate-limit rules.

Gates at `9ffafde`, with main `d4f5f18` merged ([gates-seg2b.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a281674660f311387ef68b782912cae4c99987c5/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg2b.txt)). All exit 0:
- lint;
- typecheck;
- spec:parse;
- `vitest run --changed origin/main` (1918 passed, 1 skipped);
- `e2e:affected`. The i18n change forced the full suite: 1181 passed.

**Merge of main `b57b4a0` (#1500, #1505)** at `0f8ad77`, resolved keeping both sides ([seg2b-merge-main.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/06c35b0de08fefbe65d80ddac13f34643d3d032e/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-merge-main.txt)):
- `requestMerge` runs main's #1487 refusal first (a merge step already pending, claimed or waiting for quota), before any phase write or GitHub read; the API path follows.
- `githubPrOf` takes the todo row and resolves the project through `projectOfTodo`, so the API merge, the merge-step tail and the #1150 CI entry treat a project as GitHub only when it belongs to the todo's team.
- New tests in `pr-merge-api.test.ts`: 2b-M3 (a todo pointing at another team's GitHub project takes the merge-step path and sends no GitHub request; fails on 2b before the merge), and pins 2b-M1 (a cancelled or reset card gets no API merge) and 2b-M2 (a close or reset during the PR read sends no PUT and writes nothing). D31 now expects #1487's refusal text.

Gates on `0f8ad77` ([gates-seg2b.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/06c35b0de08fefbe65d80ddac13f34643d3d032e/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg2b.txt), dated section), all exit 0: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (1952 passed), `e2e:affected` (full suite, 1181 passed). The full server suite passes: 128 files, 2116 passed.

Reviews ([seg2b-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a281674660f311387ef68b782912cae4c99987c5/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-reviews.txt)):
- /simplify, one pass.
- /code-review at medium, seven passes in all. Every finding was fixed tests first, except those listed in Risk.
- /security-review: no finding at confidence 8 or above. The skill picked up another checkout's diff, so this branch's diff was reviewed by hand under its rules.

**Round 2, from the pr-gate run at `06c35b0`** (go, six suggestions; [verdict and dispositions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/efea0f2616e2fce136556c3a230e54c04c1f9168/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-r2-reviews.txt)):
- The squash title came from the PR title verbatim, so anyone who can retitle the PR could put a closing keyword on the default branch and close an unrelated issue. A title that matches the closing shape is now replaced, and the body is always pacman's own (see What). GitHub's "Linking a pull request to an issue" keyword list, reference forms and commit-message rule are quoted in the reviews file.
- The closes line is built from the task row re-read after the PR GET (D43, from /code-review).
- 2b-D13c now asserts the PUT, the row before the sweep and the sweep's PR read; the old version passed against two no-op implementations, the new one fails both.
- The test-file header puts rate limits under D40 (409).
- Main `c99de10` (#1503) is merged; the one conflict, the write list in `lib/github.ts`'s header, now names all four writes.

Round 2 red/green ([seg2b-r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/efea0f2616e2fce136556c3a230e54c04c1f9168/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-r2-red-green.txt)): tests ahead of code, 14 failed of 297; after the fix 297 of 297; D43 1 failed of 298, then 298 of 298. Mutations on the round 2 tree ([seg2b-mutations-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/efea0f2616e2fce136556c3a230e54c04c1f9168/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-mutations-2.txt)): 71 of 71 caught, including the title rule, the always-sent body, the team-scoped routing and the #1487-first ordering. Gates on `efea0f2` ([gates-seg2b-r2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/efea0f2616e2fce136556c3a230e54c04c1f9168/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg2b-r2.txt)), all exit 0: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (2059 passed, 1 skipped), `e2e:affected` (full suite, 1181 passed).

**Round 3, from the pr-gate run at `efea0f2`** (go, six suggestions; dispositions in [seg2b-r3-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ff4c424724f5f12641aad7677d5527ca02f63675/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-r3-reviews.txt)):
- The adoption rejection floor counted only PRs by authors with write access, so a newer PR closed unmerged but opened by another login was ignored and an older merged PR could be re-adopted. The floor now counts all of the build's own PRs; the author rule still decides which PR may be adopted. Round 2's test [2b-P7g] pinned the regressed behaviour and is flipped; [2b-P7h] is new.
- A failed PR read on the merge path (404, 429, rate-limited 403, 5xx, non-JSON or array 200, timeout, network error) answers 409 with one GET, no PUT and no row ([2b-D44a/c/d]). These passed at once and are pins.
- Rate limits answering 409 is the user's decision of 2026-10-22 ([comment](https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1403#issuecomment-6344983763)); the code comment, test header and spec 02 cite it.
- Main `2ff0b93` is merged, with no conflict.

Round 3 red/green ([seg2b-r3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ff4c424724f5f12641aad7677d5527ca02f63675/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-r3-red-green.txt)): the floor tests failed 4 before the fix; `pr-merge-api.test.ts` and `pr-reconcile.test.ts` then pass 305 of 305. Mutations ([seg2b-r3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ff4c424724f5f12641aad7677d5527ca02f63675/docs/verify/1403/seg2b-r3-mutations.txt)): 8 of 8 caught. /code-review at medium found six items; four are fixed, two are in Risk. Gates on `6873877` ([gates-seg2b-r3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ff4c424724f5f12641aad7677d5527ca02f63675/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg2b-r3.txt)), all exit 0: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (2086 passed, 1 skipped), `e2e:affected` (full suite, 1182 passed).

After #1525 merged, main `f8483f7` is merged in at `8054460`; the only conflict was spec 28 §8's P2 and P3 rows. Gates on the merge ([gates-seg2b-r4.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0d67951e35e8b64db780c3ecf9375b71f2659f16/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg2b-r4.txt)), all exit 0: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (2089 passed, 1 skipped), `e2e:affected` (full suite, 1182 passed).

This is the first server-side write to GitHub with the team token that merges code.

## Upstream

No dependency. GitHub REST `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge`, as ADR 0021 D2 names it. GitHub's page also recommends an async merge endpoint; design D uses the synchronous one.

## Risk

One-way-ish: this changes how a person's merge works for GitHub-form tasks with a PR.

The live REST merge has only run against a fake GitHub. The real-host leg, a merge from pacman landing on GitHub, is 待宿主.

Kept as decided:
- Squash only. A repository that disallows squash returns GitHub's 405 message.
- A merge step queued before the upgrade blocks the API merge and the reconcile until a machine claims it.
- MEMBER and COLLABORATOR may have only read access. A private org member can show as CONTRIBUTOR to an anonymous reader; adoption then falls back to segment 1's close behaviour.
- A pending verify step can be claimed while the merge request runs (up to 15 s). Closing that needs a check in the claim path in `machines.ts`, which is on the security list, so it goes to a follow-up.
- A real 403 refusal on the last unit of quota is reported as rate-limited. GitHub's message is still shown.

From round 2:
- PRs are opened by the agent with the machine's `gh` login; the team token is only the push credential. If that login is a bot or app (association NONE or CONTRIBUTOR), every merge press answers 409 and writes nothing. A review card can still finish through a merge on GitHub and the reconcile; a failed card cannot, and the person closes or reruns it. Every PR on this repository so far is OWNER-authored.
- An unclear answer (timeout, network error, 5xx, unreadable 200) moves a failed card back to review even if GitHub refused; the PR stays open at the review gate (spec 02 A6).
- Closing keywords in the PR description are not covered. GitHub's docs say they close the issue, while this repository's record (CLAUDE.md, PRs 477 to 480, 487, 488) shows body-only keywords did not. Blocking on them means reading the PR body and refusing the merge; that is a decision for the user and needs a live check.
- The title check over-matches (for example "Fix CVE-2024-1"); the cost is only the PR title.

From round 3:
- ADR 0021 D2 says the squash title is the PR title and the body always ends with the closes line. The code now follows spec 02 instead (title replaced on a closing shape; body `closes #N` only for a same-repo issue, otherwise `Merged by pacman.`). The ADR is a protected path, so it is not edited here. Proposed note for you to add to ADR 0021 or a short ADR 0021a: "D2 message clause, revised 2026-10-22 (#1403 segment 2b, PR #1509): the squash title is `<PR title> (#n)`, or `Merge pull request #n` when the PR title carries a GitHub closing keyword with a reference. The body is the closes line only when the task came from an issue of the same repository, otherwise `Merged by pacman.`; it is always sent, so GitHub never falls back to the PR body. Spec 02 holds the full rule."
- Someone without write access can open and then close a PR on the build's branch, which raises the rejection floor and blocks adoption. The card then fails and waits for a person, which is the cheaper mistake; GitHub's branch PR list does not say who closed a PR.
- A failed PR read gives a generic message without the rate-limit reset time, because `githubPull` reports every read failure as null.
- With `PACMAN_TOKEN` unset, the merge route cannot tell a person from an agent on a machine that reaches the server port. This auth scope predates the PR, but the route now writes to the default branch.

Not done: pr-gate suggestion 1 from #1489, adoption of a PR opened after the close was reported. It needs new state and a new rule.

Segment 3 is still open: checks by head SHA, BEHIND and DIRTY handling, and exact step finish times.

This PR changes the merge path and is about 2,200 lines outside `docs/verify/`, so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Pressing merge on a GitHub-form task with a PR merges through REST with `sha` and squash; the card is done only when GitHub says merged (`pr-merge-api.test.ts`, red/green)
- [x] A refusal, including a rate limit, answers 409 with GitHub's message and writes nothing; an unclear answer writes one row and the reconcile finishes (`pr-merge-api.test.ts`)
- [x] Other forms keep the merge step; queued merge steps do not finish a GitHub build that has a PR
- [x] Adoption requires the PR author's write association; the pr-gate pins from #1489 (`pr-reconcile.test.ts`)
- [x] 51 of 51 and 7 of 7 mutations caught (`seg2b-mutations.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected (full suite) pass (`gates-seg2b.txt`), again after merging main `b57b4a0`
- [x] A PR title with a closing shape never reaches the squash title, and the body is always pacman's own (`pr-merge-api.test.ts` D41, D42, D2; 71 of 71 mutations, `seg2b-mutations-2.txt`)
- [x] Round 3: the rejection floor counts every own PR, and a failed PR read refuses without a PUT (`pr-reconcile.test.ts` 2b-P7g/h, `pr-merge-api.test.ts` 2b-D44; 8 of 8 mutations, `seg2b-r3-mutations.txt`; gates `gates-seg2b-r3.txt`)
- [x] Merge with #1505 keeps #1487's refusal first and team-scoped GitHub routing (`pr-merge-api.test.ts` 2b-M1 to 2b-M3, `seg2b-merge-main.txt`)

## Issues

Part of #1403 (segment 2b). Segment 3 carries the closing line for #1403, so this squash body has none.

Squash with this message:

```
server(1403): pressing merge on a GitHub task merges its PR through the API (#1509)

For a GitHub-form build with a recorded PR, requestMerge merges the PR
with PUT pulls/n/merge, sha set to the build's last pushed checkpoint,
squash, the PR title with its number (pacman's own title when the PR
title has a closing shape), and a body of its own that carries closes
#N only for an issue of the same repository. It checks the phase, the current build, the
PR's identity, author, base and head first and writes nothing before
the answer. Merged: a merged row and done. Refused, rate limits
included: 409 with GitHub's message. No clear answer: one row, and the
reconcile finishes. Merges in flight block the sweep; queued merge
steps no longer finish such a build; other forms keep the merge step.
Adoption requires the author's write association, and a PR closed
unmerged on the branch blocks adopting older ones. Rate-limit headers
share one parser. A merge step already in flight is refused first, and
only a GitHub project of the todo's own team takes the API path.
