mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 1 of 3 for #1406 (bootstrap phase P5a, `docs/spec/28` on #1410): the server takes `ready-for-agent` issues from GitHub on its own, under ADR 0021 D5. The plan and the failure modes are in the ticket comment (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1406#issuecomment-6311590280).

- `apps/server/src/services/issue-intake.ts` is a new loop in the scheduler family, every 5 minutes, beside the CI grind's timer (`scheduler.ts`); `tick()` stays free of network reads. It is off unless `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` is `1`, `true` or `yes` (`config.ts`, `packages/shared/src/brand.ts`), and the server logs at startup whether it is on. Per team with a GitHub token (no anonymous reads) and per project whose `githubRepo` is a well-formed `owner/repo`:
  - The project is skipped before any import when the team's chief is not bound to an agent with a model (`chiefBinding` in `chief.ts`, the same chief row and check `sendChiefMessage` uses), so no card is created that `orchestrateTodo` would refuse.
  - A conditional list read of open issues labeled `ready-for-agent`, oldest first (`sort=created&direction=asc`, 100 per page, following `rel="next"` for up to 3 pages; a 304 reuses the cached list). Pull requests in the list are skipped.
  - In-flight cap: at most 3 `github-issue` tasks per project outside done and closed (failed counts); only the remaining room is imported, oldest first, and the list is not read when the project is full.
  - D5 per candidate: the issue's events are read, the newest `labeled` event for `ready-for-agent` decides, and its actor must be a person (a label applied through a GitHub App, `performed_via_github_app` set, is not taken and is logged with the app's slug) with triage, write, maintain or admin on the repository (`collaborators/{login}/permission`, read through `role_name`, cached 15 minutes). The events read follows up to 5 pages; a later `unlabeled`, a history longer than that, a malformed event, or any failed read means the issue is not taken this sweep. A 429, or a 403 with rate-limit signals, on any intake read stops that team's sweep for the run and logs the reset time.
  - Import through `importGithubIssue` (409 when the issue already has a task, team-wide) with `createdBy` set to the team chief's bound agent id, which marks the task as the poller's (the REST import and the webhook keep the seed user), then `orchestrateTodo`. A failed orchestrate is retried on later sweeps, at most 3 attempts in all, and stops when the task has left todo, a person has started it, or the chief is now bound to another agent; the count is kept in memory.
  - An issue closed on GitHub closes a task the poller imported (its `createdBy` is the team chief's current bound agent) through `transitionTodos(..., 'closed')`, the close funnel that stops the task's active steps (#1445, #1451), but only when this process saw the issue open first (at import or in an earlier read) and the newest `closed` event's actor has triage or above. A task imported by hand from an issue that was already closed, or any issue first seen closed after a restart, is never closed by the poller, and a reopened task stays open. A task in review, or any task with a build that delivered a PR, is left to the PR reconcile of #1414, so a merge that closes the issue ends in done rather than closed. While the chief is unbound nothing is reconciled for that team, and what the poller saw open is kept until it is bound again. The phase is read again right before the write.
  - The sweep never overlaps itself, logs one tally line (`issue intake sweep`), and logs `issue intake sweep failed` with the reason when something outside the per-team handling throws.
- `apps/server/src/services/github-issues.ts`: `importGithubIssue` takes an in-process claim on team and sourceRef before its GitHub reads and releases it in `finally`, so the webhook and the poller importing the same issue at once give one task and one 409. `todo.sourceRef` has no unique index; the claim covers one server process.
- `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`: four reads in the issue section after `githubRepoLabels` (`githubOpenIssuesWithLabel`, `githubIssueEvents`, `githubCollaboratorPermission`, `githubIssueState`); the events read keeps `performed_via_github_app` as `viaApp`, and the "issue intake candidate taken" log line names the labeler and `viaApp` with a local conditional GET. They sit outside the regions #1414 rewrites; `git merge-tree` against #1414, #1420 and #1421 shows no conflict.
- `transitionTodos` takes a `Pick` of the deps it uses, so the scheduler's deps reach it. `issueIntakeRunOf(config, run)` in `scheduler.ts` decides whether the run slot is passed and logs the on/off line.
- spec 28 §8 marks P0 (#1410) merged and fills the P5 row with this PR.
- `README.md` and `README.zh.md` document `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE`: off by default, the D5 rule, the cap, the close rule, the 300-issue window, and that issues already labeled are taken oldest first, so check what is labeled before turning it on.

The webhook's `pacman` trigger is unchanged here; #1477 (#1459) makes it follow D5 on top of this PR. Segment 2 (#1467, merged) makes the chief and MCP `issues` / `pull_requests` / `workflow_runs` tools read GitHub; segment 3 (#1475) covers the repo rules for the in-product agent. PR review comments into fix rounds (P5b) need P4.

## Verified

The GitHub facts were read from the REST docs and the OpenAPI description first, and the list and events shapes captured from this repository ([api-notes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/api-notes.txt); fixtures under `apps/server/test/fixtures/issue-intake/`, copies in `docs/verify/1406/fixtures/`). The permission endpoint could not be captured: this container's proxy refuses that path, so its fixture is GitHub's OpenAPI example and the notes say so.

Old leg, the new tests against unchanged sources ([p5a1-red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-red.txt)): the concurrency tests in `github-issues.test.ts` and `webhook.test.ts` get two tasks instead of one, and the intake file cannot load its module; with an exports-only stub of the module, 44 of 50 intake tests fail (the 6 that pass are negative cases a no-op satisfies, and the mutations cover them):

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/issue-intake.test.ts apps/server/test/github-issues.test.ts apps/server/test/webhook.test.ts
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
      Tests  2 failed | 45 passed (47)
(exports-only stub)
      Tests  44 failed | 6 passed (50)
```

New leg ([p5a1-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-green.txt)):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  97 passed (97)
```

Mutations ([p5a1-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-mutations.txt)), each one rule undone alone, each turning a test red: the labeler permission check, the newest-event rule, a later `unlabeled`, an events page that is not the last, the cap, failed counting toward the cap, the pull request skip, the chief precondition, the concurrent claim, review left alone on close, the phase read before the close write, the overlap guard and the permission cache.

The switch, tests first ([p5a1-optin-red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-optin-red.txt), [p5a1-optin-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-optin-green.txt)): 16 of 18 fail before it (config field and env slot missing; the two scheduler cases without the slot pass on both sides), 18 of 18 after. The real server started in a scratch `PACMAN_HOME` on port 8794, then stopped by its PID ([p5a1-optin-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-optin-live.txt)):

```
(PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE unset)
{"level":30,"issueIntake":false,"msg":"github issue intake off (set PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE=1 to enable)"}
no 'issue intake sweep' line: 0 matches
(PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE=1)
{"level":30,"issueIntake":true,"msg":"github issue intake on (PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE)"}
{"level":30,"teams":0,"projects":0,"skipped":0,"listNotModified":0,"candidates":0,"claimed":0,"atCap":0,"notEligible":0,"unverifiable":0,"imported":0,"orchestrated":0,"closed":0,"closeSkipped":0,"errors":0,"msg":"issue intake sweep"}
```


Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 on this PR (no-go at `f911447`, one blocking finding both skeptics confirmed), at `6fe338a` ([p5a1-r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a31396606c105affc60bdab8a03866057c20546a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r2-red-green.txt), [p5a1-r2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a31396606c105affc60bdab8a03866057c20546a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r2-mutations.txt), [gates-p5a1-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a31396606c105affc60bdab8a03866057c20546a/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1-3.txt), [p5a1-r2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a31396606c105affc60bdab8a03866057c20546a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r2-live.txt), [p5a1-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a31396606c105affc60bdab8a03866057c20546a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-reviews.txt), [pr-gate-1461-run1-f911447.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a31396606c105affc60bdab8a03866057c20546a/docs/verify/1406/pr-gate-1461-run1-f911447.json)). The close reconcile closed every `github-issue` task whose issue read closed, including a task a person imported by hand from an issue that was already closed (the import dialog offers a closed filter), and closed it again after each reopen. It now closes a task only on an open-to-closed change this process saw, and only when the newest `closed` event's actor has triage or above (the same check and cache as the labeler); a read failure, an incomplete history, a deleted actor or an outside closer means no close, counted in `closeSkipped`. From the suggestions: an error outside the per-team handling is logged (`issue intake sweep failed`) instead of being swallowed; the label list follows `rel="next"` (api.github.com only) for up to 3 pages, reads full pages without `If-None-Match`, and counts `listTruncated`; `/code-review` then found that the events read stopped at the first page, so a long ticket's labeler or closer was never seen, and both reads now follow up to 5 pages; the on/off decision moved into `issueIntakeRunOf`, which `index.ts` calls and a test pins. spec 28 §8 marks P0 merged and fills the P5 row. With the round 2 tests against the `f911447` sources, 16 of 87 fail (the rest are regression pins); against the pre-review head, the events-paging tests fail 3 of 90; at the head the three files pass 137 of 137, and 30 single-rule mutations, including the round 1 rules re-checked, each turn a test red. Gates at `9f58f10`: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` has the one root-only failure, confirmed identical on main. The live start shows the off line with no sweep when unset, and the on line and a tally with `listTruncated` when set.

Round 3, after pr-gate run 2 (go at `a313966`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1461-run2-a313966.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/pr-gate-1461-run2-a313966.json)), at `4cb207e` ([p5a1-r3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r3-red-green.txt), [p5a1-r3b-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r3b-red-green.txt), [p5a1-r3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r3-mutations.txt), [p5a1-r3b-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r3b-mutations.txt), [p5a1-r3-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r3-reviews.txt), [gates-p5a1-4.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1-4.txt), [gates-p5a1-5.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/69722cc9fea398bf085e89ceda44ad781081cb61/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1-5.txt)). The run traced two real defects. A building or failed task whose PR a maintainer merged with a closing reference was closed instead of left to the PR reconcile; the close reconcile now skips any task with a build that carries a PR, checking every build of the task, since a rerun gets a new build without one. A failed orchestrate after the import left the task in todo for good, holding a cap slot; it is retried as described above. The reconcile also covered tasks a person or the webhook imported, wider than the ticket; it now takes only the poller's tasks, marked by `createdBy`, so the scope survives a restart. Pins the run asked for: the newest closed event decides, an unrelated label removed after `ready-for-agent` does not block, the same-second tie-break by event id, a task a person reopens is not closed again, and the issue body appears in the chief thread's user message and not in `composeChiefSystemPrompt`. Each red leg ran on a tests-only commit on this branch: 7 of 103 at `80def1d` and 3 of 113 at `fe3654d` against the earlier sources, plus 4 and 2 and 2 and 1 for the code-review passes; issue-intake now has 119 tests, and issue-intake, github-issues and webhook pass 166 of 166. 29 mutations (20 and 9) each turn a test red. Gates at `4cb207e`: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2616 with the one root-only failure. Four `/code-review` passes found 47 items; the ones fixed and the ones left, each with its reason, are in `p5a1-r3-reviews.txt` and `gates-p5a1-5.txt`.

Round 4, after pr-gate run 3 (go at `69722cc`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1461-run3-69722cc.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/22cf8db1970cc20f438e9b9e19024aca6f958bca/docs/verify/1406/pr-gate-1461-run3-69722cc.json)), at `5cf6e92` ([p5a1-r4-merge.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/22cf8db1970cc20f438e9b9e19024aca6f958bca/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r4-merge.txt), [p5a1-r4-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/22cf8db1970cc20f438e9b9e19024aca6f958bca/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r4-red-green.txt), [p5a1-r4-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/22cf8db1970cc20f438e9b9e19024aca6f958bca/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r4-mutations.txt), [p5a1-r4-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/22cf8db1970cc20f438e9b9e19024aca6f958bca/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r4-reviews.txt), [gates-p5a1-6.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/22cf8db1970cc20f438e9b9e19024aca6f958bca/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1-6.txt)). The branch took main at `dabef48` (#1420, #1411, #1467, #1456) by a merge commit without conflicts; 302 tests over the intake, GitHub, webhook, orchestration, chief and vocabulary files pass on the merge. The close reconcile skips a split parent whose children are not all done or closed, so the last child's done can still move the parent to done. Source refs compare without case in `claimedSourceRefs` and the in-process claim, so `github:Acme/App#5` and `github:acme/app#5` are one issue. A rate-limited read stops the team's sweep (one rejected read, then the team is skipped). A label applied through a GitHub App, with or without a slug, is not taken. A 502 import neither ends the project's sweep nor marks the issue seen open; an unreadable later list page imports nothing past the pages read. Spec 28 §8's P5 row names #1467 as merged. Red 20 of 188 on `68d6dbc` and 22 of 189 on `fb1f23d` (tests only), green 189 of 189; 15 of 15 mutations caught. Gates at `5cf6e92`: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0, and `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2819 (the root-only runner-brief case is no longer selected since main has #1458). `/code-review` on the branch's own changes found nothing; `p5a1-r4-reviews.txt` lists every earlier finding left as it is, each with its reason.

Round 1 gates ([gates-p5a1.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1.txt) at `645640f`, [gates-p5a1-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f9114471a47ab384eed15be62306575c387d3e55/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1-2.txt) at `7b2c1f5`): `pnpm lint` (1 info, the existing `noUselessFragments` note in `machines-page.tsx`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (2 specs, 8 passed) exit 0. `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 1235 tests at `645640f`; at `7b2c1f5` the shared env name pulls in 248 files and 2564 pass with one failure, `runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败", which makes a directory read-only and fails the same way on main when run as root, as this container does. `/simplify` and `/code-review` found nothing to change after their fixes; no file on the AGENTS.md `/security-review` list is touched.

## Upstream

No dependency polls GitHub issues here. The rules come from the GitHub REST docs, quoted with URLs in `api-notes.txt`: the issues list returns pull requests marked by `pull_request`; issue events carry `labeled` and `unlabeled` with `actor.login`, `label.name` and `created_at`, paged with a `Link` header; `collaborators/{username}/permission` answers 200 or 404 and needs only Metadata read, and its `permission` field maps maintain to write and triage to read, so the intake reads `role_name`; a 304 to an authorized conditional request does not count against the primary rate limit. Events were chosen over the timeline API because the timeline also returns comment bodies.

## Risk

Two-way door, and off by default: nothing changes until `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` is set. Once it is set, a team with a GitHub connection and a bound chief gets its oldest labeled issues imported and dispatched, up to 3 open per project; this repository labels most issues `ready-for-agent` for the issue-label gate, so the README says to check the labels first. Spec 28 P8 is where it would be turned on for real (drill repository first).

Left as they are, with the reason:
- The claim against double import holds within one server process; a unique index on `todo(teamId, sourceRef)` would cover several instances but needs a migration, which belongs with the migration-numbering rules at merge time.
- A failed orchestrate is retried at most 3 times; the count lives in memory, so a restart forgets a task that still waits, which a person then starts.
- The poller's tasks show the chief's agent as their creator. Rebinding the chief to another agent leaves the tasks taken under the old one outside the close reconcile.
- The per-project cap of 3 counts every open `github-issue` task, including ones imported by hand or by the webhook, which the reconcile does not close; they hold slots until a person closes them. The cap limits work in flight per project whatever its source.
- A closed task keeps its sourceRef, so an issue reopened and labeled again is not imported again (409).
- An issue with more than 500 events is never taken, and only the 300 oldest labeled issues are read each sweep (`listTruncated` counts a cut); a deleted or transferred issue (404, 410) leaves its task as it is.
- The close reconcile only acts on changes this process saw, so an issue closed while the server was down leaves its task open until a person closes it.
- D5 vets who applied the label, not the text: an issue body or title edited after labeling is imported as it stands, as data (spec 28: the merge gate and D4 are the guard). A label applied through a GitHub App is not taken, so an agent session holding the owner's authorization cannot feed the intake its own issues; a person relabels such an issue to have it taken.
- A task in review, or with a delivered PR, is left to #1414's PR reconcile, which is not on main yet; until it is, such a task stays as it is when its issue closes.
- No end-to-end run against GitHub with a real team token: the proxy refuses the permission endpoint, so the import path is shown by tests over captured shapes and the live run above shows the switch. The run on a long-lived instance with a drill repository is a host leg (spec 28 §8, 待宿主).
- `intakeGet` in `lib/github.ts` is a second conditional GET beside #1414's `conditionalGetJson`; they merge into one after #1414 lands, to keep the two PRs free of conflicts now.
- The webhook trigger follows D5 in #1477 (#1459), stacked on this PR.
- The close reconcile's two correlated NOT EXISTS checks (delivered PR, open children) have no index; they run once per sweep, every 5 minutes.
- A 429 on an import's own detail or labels read counts as that import's failure; the next candidate's events read then stops the team.
- Code-review findings left as they are, each with its reason, are listed in `p5a1-r4-reviews.txt`.

The patch is 9,626 lines (5,015 outside `docs/verify/`) across 58 files, over ADR 0021 D4's 800-line cap, and edits `docs/spec/28` and the READMEs outside the auto-merge set, so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Intake filter unit tests: label, labeler permission, newest event, already imported, in-flight cap (`issue-intake.test.ts`, groups 1 to 14)
- [x] Webhook and poller importing the same issue at once give one task (`github-issues.test.ts`, `webhook.test.ts`, `issue-intake.test.ts`)
- [x] Close reconcile: only an observed open-to-closed change by a closer with triage or above closes a task; a task imported from a closed issue, or reopened, stays open (round 2, `p5a1-r2-red-green.txt`); only the poller's tasks, never one with a delivered PR (round 3, `p5a1-r3-red-green.txt`, `p5a1-r3b-red-green.txt`)
- [x] A failed orchestrate after the import is retried, bounded (round 3, `p5a1-r3-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Split parents, ref case, rate limits and app-applied labels handled (round 4, `p5a1-r4-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Off by default; on with `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE`; the server says which at startup (`p5a1-optin-*.txt`)
- [x] Mutations: each of 13 rules in round 1, 30 in round 2 and 29 in round 3 and 15 in round 4 turns a test red when undone (`p5a1-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r2-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r3-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r3b-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r4-mutations.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case (`gates-p5a1.txt` to `gates-p5a1-6.txt`)

Ticket items outside this segment, tracked on #1406: the chief read tools (segment 2, #1467), repo rules for the in-product agent (segment 3, #1475), the webhook trigger under D5 (#1459, #1477, stacked on this PR), PR comment feedback (P5b after P4); the drill-repository run is 待宿主.

## Issues

mergedPulls.title: server(1403): reconcile review-phase PRs merged or closed on GitHub
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 1 of 3 for #1403 (bootstrap phase P2, `docs/spec/28` on #1410): a todo in review learns what happened to its PR on GitHub.

Today a GitHub-form todo stays in review after its PR is merged on GitHub, because nothing reads the PR once the CI grind (`apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts`, building phase only) hands it over. A PR closed without merging leaves the card in review as well.

- `ci-loop.ts` gets a second candidate set in the same 60 s sweep: builds that have a PR number, whose todo is in `review`, that are the todo's current build (`todo.latestBuildId`), and that have no step in flight (claimed, or queued or waiting for quota other than a verify or review step). An older build's PR never decides a newer build's fate, a merge step that is merging the PR finishes the todo itself, and an offline or quota-blocked Verifier does not pin the card. The checks run again after each network read. Each candidate gets one conditional GET of `pulls/{n}`; a PR already read as merged is not read again, since a merge is final, unless that response lacked the base or head fields the merge check needs (it is then read again under the same throttles). Without a GitHub connection a PR is read at most every five minutes, the reconcile spends at most 20 anonymous requests an hour of its own and stops when it and the grind together reach 50 (GitHub allows 60 per IP; the rest is left to the #931 / #1217 guards), a pulls read starts only with room left for the compare it may need, and the PR read longest ago goes first.
  - Merged into the default branch, by anyone: a system row `PR #n 已在 GitHub 合并（合并提交 abc1234，由 <login> 合并）`, then `finishTodoDone`. When the build's last pushed checkpoint (any step but review, ordered by when the step last checked in) is not contained in the merged head (`compare/{checkpoint}...{head}?per_page=1` is not ahead or identical, or the commit is unknown to GitHub), the merge missed later work: one hint names the commit and the card stays in review. A merge into, or a close of, a PR with another base, or a response without a head sha or base, leaves the card in review (with one hint for another base).
  - Closed without merge into the default branch, and still closed at the next read 50 s or more later (closing and reopening a PR to rerun CI is common; an open read, a skipped or failed read resets the count, and the time is when each read happened, not when the sweep started): a closed row, `build.errorMessage` (a person most likely decided against the change; restart opens a new branch, spec 23 R3), and `failed`.
  - Each outcome is reported once per round. A round starts at the build's latest build or plan step, so a #931 rework round on the same build starts fresh. The markers are this round's completion row (written by the merge step or the reconcile) and the reconcile's own closed row. A person who moves the card back into review after the report keeps it there; a finish by hand before the reconcile saw the outcome is followed by one report. No clock is read, so a PR merged the moment CI went green (GitHub auto-merge) still finishes a card that reaches review afterwards.
  - compare results are cached per PR and commit pair. A 404 or an unreadable compare is read again after ten minutes; two failed reads in a row leave one hint, written only if the card is still in review with no step in flight and no completion row this round. A checkpoint that is not a 40-hex sha never reaches the URL or the hint text and takes no anonymous slot. Hints are written once per round and quote branch names as data.
  - Open, unreadable (including a response without a boolean `merged`), or phase changed during a read: nothing is written. A sweep that starts while the last one runs returns at once. Cache rows of PRs that left review or the grind are dropped. The sweep log counts the reconcile (`reviewPending`, `reviewSkipped`, `reviewUnreadable`, `reviewForeign`, `merged`, `closedUnmerged`, `hinted`, `settledBefore`) apart from the grind.
  - Only the build's own PR: before any write the pull's head repository must be its base repository (compared by repository id, so a renamed or transferred repository still matches) and its head ref the build's conversation branch. The daemon finds the PR number with `gh pr list --head <branch>`, which matches the branch name only, so on a public repo a fork PR with the same branch name can be the number on the build. A mismatch, or a head repository that GitHub reports as null (a deleted fork), writes nothing (no done, no failed) and leaves one hint per round; a response without the head ref or the base repository id counts as unreadable and is read again. Text from GitHub that reaches a system row (branch names, the merger's login, the merge sha) is stripped of control characters and cut to 100 characters.
- `apps/server/src/services/builds.ts`: the merge step's done tail moves into `finishTodoDone`, shared by the merge step and the reconcile. It checks that the card can reach done (a person may have closed it while the merge step ran) before touching anything, stops the build's unclaimed verify / review steps, sets done, writes the completion row (`DONE_ROW`, every time, as before), and advances split waves. `roundStart` and `hasMessageRow` back the per-round markers. `requestMerge` and the AI review action re-read the phase after their await and refuse when the reconcile finished the card meanwhile. Step events go through quota-wait's `publishStepRow`. `phase.ts` names the reconcile as a review -> done / failed producer, and `docs/spec/02` §4.2 describes it next to the main sequence and in the failure list.
- `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`: `githubPull` reads `state`, `merged`, `merge_commit_sha`, `merged_by.login`, `head.sha`, `head.ref`, `head.repo.id`, `base.ref`, `base.repo.id` and `base.repo.default_branch` with `If-None-Match`; `githubPullState` (#931) is now a projection of it. It and `githubCommitCheckRuns` share one conditional GET. `githubCompareStatus` asks for one page and answers `invalid` without a request when either commit is not a 40-hex sha.
- The checks path and the new path share `githubTarget` (which goes through #1468's `githubRepoOfProject`: a `githubRepo` that is not owner/repo, or has a `.` or `..` segment, is refused), `tokenFor` and `hasActiveStep`. Two changes reach the CI grind: its candidates are limited to the todo's current build (since #1150 a newer build in flight still had the old PR ground), an unclaimed verify or review step no longer holds it back, and a step of another kind waiting for quota (a fix step, or a #931 rework build step) counts as in flight, so the grind adds no second fix step behind it. `ci-loop.test.ts`'s fixture now sets `todo.latestBuildId`, which every grind test depends on.

Segments 2 and 3 cover the human merge through the API with `sha`, the review-gate wake text (G9), checks by head SHA, and DIRTY/BEHIND.

## Verified

New tests first, `apps/server/test/pr-reconcile.test.ts`, run on main `89cc029` with only the test file added ([red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39990abc5fe6a8860f26414a96b640c046240816/docs/verify/1403/red.txt)):

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run test/pr-reconcile.test.ts
     × ① merged on GitHub → todo done, merge sha in a system row, celebration row
     × ② closed without merge → todo failed with the cause on the build
     × ⑤ phase moved by a person during the network window → no write
     × ⑦ after done, a second sweep does not touch the todo again
      Tests  4 failed | 6 passed (10)
```

The six that pass on main are the "nothing changes" guards (③ open, ④ 429/404/502, ⑥ older closed PR, building phase untouched); they hold the new code to the same outcome.

Same tests on this branch, plus the whole server project ([green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39990abc5fe6a8860f26414a96b640c046240816/docs/verify/1403/green.txt)):

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run test/pr-reconcile.test.ts test/ci-loop.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  30 passed (30)

$ pnpm exec vitest run --project @xiechimon/pacman
 Test Files  110 passed (110)
      Tests  1140 passed | 1 skipped (1141)
```

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 on this PR (head `373d42e`, `go: false`): the review candidates were keyed on `latestPrBuild`, so a rerun or restart whose newest build has no PR (the #1217 guard tells the agent not to open one after a merged PR; the daemon's PR probe can also come back empty) had its fate decided by the older PR; and the reconcile raced an in-flight merge step, writing the completion row twice. New tests on `373d42e` with only the test files changed ([fix-red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ea2b9f883b8962e9de0b99ab8881ed5d6277b705/docs/verify/1403/fix-red.txt)):

```
     × ⑧a the todo's current build has no PR; an older build's PR merged → nothing changes
     × ⑧b the todo's current build has no PR; an older build's PR closed → not failed
     × ⑩a a merge step in flight → reconcile does not step in
     × ⑩b finishing twice leaves one completion row
     × ⑪ anonymous: a candidate is read at most once per five minutes
     × ⑬ the merge row names who merged
     × #1403 重跑开出的新 build 是 todo 的当前 build 时，旧 PR build 不再被磨（不读 checks、不派修复步）
      Tests  7 failed | 33 passed (40)
```

At `ea2b9f8` ([fix-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ea2b9f883b8962e9de0b99ab8881ed5d6277b705/docs/verify/1403/fix-green.txt)): those two files 40/40, the server project 110 files, 1150 passed. ⑨ (two builds on one PR, #1217), ⑫a (304 reuse) and ⑫b (thrown network error, read again next sweep) pass on both sides and guard the old behavior.

Round 3, after pr-gate run 2 (head `d906440`, `go: true` with suggestions, four of them defects in this reconcile): a merge that missed a later fix-round commit, a guard that ignored `waiting_quota` and ran only before the network read, no current-build recheck before writing, and an unclaimed verify step pinning the card. New tests on `d906440` with only the test file changed ([fix3-red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c35c3498b2ddea093492161f61af149773d7117f/docs/verify/1403/fix3-red.txt)):

     × ⑮a a merge step waiting for quota counts as in flight
     × ⑮b an unclaimed verify step does not hold the reconcile

```

At `c35c349` ([fix3-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c35c3498b2ddea093492161f61af149773d7117f/docs/verify/1403/fix3-green.txt)): 26/26, the server project 110 files and 1157 passed, lint, typecheck, spec:parse and e2e:affected exit 0.

Round 4, after pr-gate run 3 (head `6792b0c`, `go: false`): the reconcile undid a person's reopen. A done card dragged back to review was finished again within a sweep, with a second merged row and a second completion row; a closed -> review drag or a failed -> review restore on a closed PR went back to failed and lost its errorMessage. The suggestions of that run added the default-branch check, stopping unclaimed gate steps, the compare cache, sha validation and the two re-reads after await. The round 4 test file, copied into a checkout of `6792b0c`, fails 11 of 42 ([r4-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/865e7f3983ea52b940fa2a8ac9cc986b9c1a1f8f/docs/verify/1403/r4-red-green.txt)):

```
     × ⑭c the checkpoint commit is unknown to GitHub (never pushed) → stays in review with a hint
     × ⑳ merged: unclaimed verify / review steps are stopped when the reconcile finishes
     × ⑳ closed: unclaimed verify / review steps are stopped when the reconcile finishes
     × ⑱a reopened done→review after the reconcile finished it → not finished again
     × ⑱b merged before the card entered review → left to the person, nothing written
     × ⑱d closed→review drag after the reconcile failed it → stays in review, errorMessage kept
     × ⑲ merged into a branch other than the default branch → stays in review, one hint
     × ㉑ the hint path reads compare once per (checkpoint, head) and writes the hint once
     × ㉕ a checkpoint that is not a 40-hex sha is not put into a request URL
     × ㉖ requestMerge: the reconcile finishes the card during the PR probe → no merge step

```

Each of 18 mutations turns at least one test red ([r5-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/d65f756d9ff0d811ad15fa71f938dc4822566003/docs/verify/1403/r5-mutations.txt); a first pass left the pulls-read recheck alive because that case also had a compare read behind it, so the case lost its checkpoint and the file is the rerun):

Each round's tests ran red against the previous head's sources and green at the new head; each round's mutations are all caught; gates ran on a clean checkout of the new head:

| Round | Head | Red at previous head | Green | Mutations | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | `82c6b50` | 7 of 73 fail | 73 | 24 of 24 | [r6-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b8d08219b078ab632b92c70d968a0e9cb74da437/docs/verify/1403/r6-red-green.txt), [r6-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b8d08219b078ab632b92c70d968a0e9cb74da437/docs/verify/1403/r6-mutations.txt), [gates-6.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b8d08219b078ab632b92c70d968a0e9cb74da437/docs/verify/1403/gates-6.txt) |

## Upstream

No equivalent exists in the current code. `githubPullState` (#931) reads `state` and `merged` for the restart decision without `merge_commit_sha` or ETag; it stays for its two callers. GitHub webhooks for pull_request events would replace the poll, but the server sits inside a tailnet that GitHub cannot reach (ci-loop.ts header), so the poll stays the transport.

## Risk

Two-way door: revert the commits and review-phase builds are ignored again. Blast radius: every GitHub-form todo in review whose current build has a PR gets one conditional GET per minute when GitHub is connected (304 responses to authorized requests do not count against the primary rate limit); without a connection the reconcile stops reading at 20 anonymous requests an hour of its own, or when it and the grind together reach 50 (the grind's reads are counted, not capped). A merged PR whose head differs from the last checkpoint adds one compare read per commit pair. The grind now skips PR builds that are not the todo's current build. A closed PR now moves the todo to `failed`, which a person used to do by hand. The merge step's done path is the same code moved into a function, plus stopping unclaimed gate steps. No migration, no wire change, no UI change. The PR edits `docs/spec/02`, outside the ADR 0021 D4 auto-merge set, so it waits for a user merge.

`/code-review` findings left as they are, with the reason:
- The per-round markers are message rows: `DONE_ROW` and the reconcile's closed text. A structured column would need a migration. If the closed text changes wording later, a card between a reported close and a reopen at that moment would see one more report.
- `DONE_ROW` names the completion row that was already product copy, emoji included; this PR gives the existing string a name and adds no new emoji text.
- `probePullState` in builds.ts (#931) keeps its own target and token code; this PR does not touch that path.
- The message table has no index on `conversationId`; the reconcile keeps positive marker lookups in memory instead of adding one, so a settled or hinted card costs no repeated scans.

`/code-review` findings from the fifth and sixth passes left as they are, with the reason:
- From the seventh pass: when the reconcile fails a card on a closed PR it stops the build's unclaimed verify step. If the PR is then reopened and the card restarted onto the same build (#931 reuse), `maybeEnqueueVerifyStep` finds that stopped row and enqueues no Verifier for the new round. On main that check already skips any build with a verify row, so a second round on one build gets no Verifier today either; verify is advisory, not a merge gate. Making it look at the round belongs with segment 2's rework of the merge path.
- The CI grind (#1150, unchanged here except for the current-build limit and the gate-step rule) reads checks by branch name and does not read the PR's state. A repo that auto-merges and deletes the head branch on merge leaves a card in building (its checks go unreadable), a PR closed during building keeps getting fix rounds until the dead-loop gate, and a grind card whose checks never read keeps adding anonymous reads. Segment 3 reads checks by head SHA and covers these.
- The merged row is written just before `finishTodoDone`, outside a transaction; only a database error between the two would repeat it on the next sweep.
- A PR merged into the old default branch, with the repository renamed before the reconcile reads it, is reported as merged into another branch; the window is one sweep unless the server was down.
- Review candidates are read one after another; with a token, a slow GitHub can push a sweep past 60 s, and the next tick is skipped.
- Close confirmation could read `closed_at` instead of a second read, which compares GitHub's clock with the server's, the kind of rule round 7 removed. The anonymous budget is counted here, not read from GitHub's `x-ratelimit-*` headers, which would also see the #931 / #1217 guard reads.
- The reconcile reads the PR number recorded on the build, which the daemon probe refreshes only when a non-review step finishes. If a person closes the build's PR and opens a new one from the same conversation branch while the card is in review, the closed read fails the card while the new PR is open, and after a restore a merge of the new PR is not seen. Segment 2, which reworks the merge step and the PR identity, takes this; listed on #1403.
- The step table has no completion time, so the last pushed checkpoint is the step that last checked in; two steps of one build that overlap and finish less than 30 s apart (one heartbeat) can be ordered wrongly, which leaves the card in review with a hint rather than finishing it. An exact `finishedAt` needs a migration.
- Round 18's ㊳b was written after the merge that routes `githubTarget` through `githubRepoOfProject`; its red leg swaps the old `githubTarget` back in, so it works as a mutation run rather than a test that came first. The rule itself is #1468's, already tested on main.
- #1468 (#1466) merged first; round 18's merge of main routes `githubTarget` through its `githubRepoOfProject`, so the reconcile and the grind refuse the same stored values the rest of the server does.
- A manual done from review does not stop unclaimed gate steps at the moment of the move. Since #1452 (now on this branch) the scheduler tick stops the pending or quota-waiting steps of a done card and a done from queued, planning or building stops them at once, so the window is one tick; closing it at claim time is outside this PR.
- `tokenFor` decrypts once per candidate per sweep; the number of candidates is the number of PR cards in building or review.
- Round 10 added tests after the rules they cover had shipped (CLAUDE.md asks for tests first); its red leg is the mutation run.
- From pr-gate run 6: a merge step queued for an Agent whose machine is offline counts as in flight (unclaimed steps wait for their machine, #1257), so a PR merged on GitHub meanwhile is reported only when that machine returns and its merge step runs. Nothing wrong is written and main never reports it; segment 2 reworks the merge step.
- The ownership check reads the PR the daemon recorded. The daemon's `gh pr list --head <branch>` probe (`apps/daemon/src/github-probe.ts`) still matches by branch name; the REST path already uses `owner:branch`. Filtering the probe by owner is a follow-up outside this PR. Until then a build whose recorded PR is a fork's stays in review with the hint, and a PR the agent opened from a branch other than the conversation branch is treated the same way, the safe direction. `mergedPrElsewhere` (#1217) also reads the recorded PR number and is not changed here.
- From pr-gate run 7: a foreign PR that is closed stays a conditional read every sweep (a 304 when nothing changed); treating it as final like a merged PR would need a rule for a PR whose base or head is later edited, so it stays a read. The live fixtures were read through this container's proxy, which adds its own GitHub credentials, so they show response shapes, not the anonymous rate limit. Some round 14 and 15 tests pin rules that were already in place (CLAUDE.md asks for tests first); their red leg is the mutation run.

Decided by the user on 2026-10-21 (option B; the `needs-decision` label is removed): pr-gate run 5 traced one path where a merge on GitHub goes unreported. In GitHub form the merge step can finish without merging the PR (it merges the default branch into the PR branch and pushes; merging the PR is left to the agent's prompt, #1403 "Current state"). The completion row it writes is this round's marker. If a person then moves the card back to review and merges the PR on GitHub, the reconcile finds the marker and leaves the card in review with no merged row (⑱c pins that a reopen after the merge step stays). Segment 2 makes the merge step merge the PR through the API with `sha`, so its completion row then always means the PR is merged; this PR adds no rule for the case.

- [x] A merge that missed the build's last commit leaves the todo in review with a hint (⑭a-c; `fix3-green.txt`)
- [x] Each outcome reported once per round: a reopen after the report stays, a rework round starts fresh, a merge before review entry still finishes the card, a merge outside the default branch leaves a hint (⑱, ⑲, ㉝, ㉞; `r7-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Unclaimed (queued or quota-blocked) gate steps stopped on the reconcile's finish and the merge step's finish (a manual done from review relies on the scheduler tick of #1452, see Risk); merge and review actions refuse after a concurrent finish (⑮c, ⑳, ㉖, ㉖b, ㊺)
- [x] Request budget: one sweep at a time, per-PR and process-wide anonymous limits shared fairly, compare backoff (⑪, ㉑, ㊱, ㊴, ㊸, ㊹, ㊻)
- [x] Round 9 rules: 37 of 37 mutations caught (`r9-mutations.txt`)
- [x] Round 10: the grind's gate-step rule and the compare-hint recheck held by tests, 2 of 2 mutations caught (`r10-mutations.txt`); gates at `0c5a702` (`gates-10.txt`)
- [x] Rounds 11 to 13: close confirmed over two reads, budgets split between the reconcile and the grind, done doc without a stale quota chip, merged PRs not re-read unless the response was incomplete, transition checked first; 23 of 23 mutations caught; gates at `f9f5a2f` (`r11-*`, `r12-*`, `r13-*`, `gates-13.txt`)
- [x] Round 14: a fork PR or another branch's PR recorded on the build neither finishes nor fails the card, a response without the head fields is read again, the merge step's done path and the grind's quota-waiting rule pinned; 4 of 4 mutations caught (`r14-red-green.txt`, `r14-mutations.txt`, `gates-14.txt`)
- [x] Round 15: ownership by repository id (renames and transfers keep working, a deleted fork is foreign), GitHub text bounded, parsers checked against live responses, head-sha guard, `behind` and split waves pinned; 22 of 22 mutations caught on the head sources (`r15-red-green.txt`, `r15-mutations.txt`, `r15-live-capture.txt`, `gates-15.txt`)
- [x] Round 16: a close confirmed only by the next read, every pushed checkpoint in the containment check, no already-done branch in the done funnel, one tally bucket per candidate, the base guard reached by tests, the batch sweep test without random PR numbers; 12 of 12 mutations caught (`r16-red-green.txt`, `r16-mutations.txt`, `gates-16.txt`)
- [x] Round 17: a closed PR acts only when its base is the default branch, checkpoints ordered by when the step last checked in, format characters stripped, the realistic #1217 shape pinned; 9 of 9 mutations caught (`r17-red-green.txt`, `r17-mutations.txt`, `gates-17.txt`)

Host leg, not a task here: a PR merged in the GitHub UI moving its card to done within a minute on mea waits for the long-lived host (spec 28 §8 「待宿主」); segment 3 records a live read against the public repo from this container.

## Issues

Part of #1403, segment 1 of 3. Segment 3 carries the closing line for #1403; this squash body has no closing keyword for it.

The branch's commit messages describe each round's rule, and later rounds replaced earlier ones, so the first commit's message (what `.[0].commit.message` returns) does not describe the code at the head. Squash with this message instead:

```
server(1403): reconcile review-phase PRs merged or closed on GitHub (#1414)

A GitHub-form todo in review now learns what happened to its PR. The
ci-loop sweep reads pulls/{n} for the todo's current build when no
step is in flight (conditional GET, not repeated once read as merged
with the fields the merge check needs; without
a GitHub connection every five minutes per PR; the reconcile stops
at 20 anonymous requests an hour of its own, or at 50 with the
grind).

- Merged into the default branch, with the merged head containing the
  build's last pushed checkpoint: a merged row, then the same done
  finish as the merge step. A merge into another branch or one that
  missed a later commit leaves the card in review with one hint.
- Closed without merge into the default branch and still closed at the
  next read, 50 s or more later: a closed row, build.errorMessage,
  failed. A closed PR with another base leaves one hint.
- Each outcome is reported once per round (round = the build's latest
  build or plan step), so a person's move back to review stays.
- finishTodoDone checks the transition first, stops unclaimed verify /
  review steps before publishing done, and writes the completion row;
  requestMerge and the AI review action re-read the phase after their
  await.
- Only the build's own PR counts: the head repository must be the
  base repository (by id) and the head ref the conversation branch;
  otherwise nothing is written and one hint is left. GitHub text in
  system rows is bounded.
- The CI grind takes only the todo's current build, and an unclaimed
  verify or review step no longer holds it back.
- githubTarget goes through githubRepoOfProject, so the reconcile and
  the grind refuse a githubRepo with a . or .. segment (#1466).
- docs/spec/02 §4.2 describes the reconcile.

mergedPulls.title: verify(1402): registry gate, drive lines in the feature maps, stack-state marks
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 2, the last, of #1402 (bootstrap phase P1, the verify-pacman CLI; `docs/spec/28` §4 P1). Segment 1 (#1411, `vp.mjs` and `vp-registry.json`) is on main as `e1b051a`. This segment adds the registry gate, puts the `vp.mjs drive` commands into the feature maps, and takes the items pr-gate run 9 on #1411 left for it (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1402#issuecomment-6314487263).

- `.claude/skills/verify-pacman/scripts/vp-registry-gate.mjs` (stdlib only) fails when:
  - a file in `scripts/` is neither a case script nor a `support` entry;
  - a `drive-<number>` script is not one of the 61 that exist today, registered or not (the ticket's rule: new probes are named for the feature);
  - the registry has no case;
  - a case script, support file or recipe path does not exist, or a status or need is unknown;
  - an `evidence.writes` path inside `docs/verify` lacks `rewrites-evidence`;
  - a `vp.mjs drive` line in a feature map names an unregistered case, or a feature with a recipe has no drive line.

  A self-test case runs it on this checkout, so the existing CI self-test step enforces it.
- The 35 feature maps with a recipe end their "How to get to it (user POV)" section with full `node .claude/skills/verify-pacman/scripts/vp.mjs drive <feature> <case>` commands for current cases and what each needs. Stale cases are listed with the reason `drive` refuses them, and a map whose feature has no current case says so. `glass-journeys.md` has a drive line per journey; `review-700.md` and `skill-import.md` gain the user-path section they lacked.
- `vp.mjs` also refuses an evidence directory inside the `docs/verify` of any `git worktree list` entry, read from the caller's directory, from `VERIFY_REPO_ROOT` and from `vp.mjs`'s own checkout, so main's `vp.mjs` run from a sibling worktree cannot overwrite that worktree's archived evidence. `docs/verify-notes` and the like stay allowed.
- Cases whose verdict depends on the stack's state are marked in the registry and `drive` checks the marks. `fresh-stack` (13 cases, `api-keys/create`, `machine-stale-sweep` and `search/project-line` among them): once a drive is recorded on the stack (`VERIFY_RUN_DIR/vp-drives.txt`, written after doctor passes, cleared by launch and cleanup), such a case is refused with "cleanup, then launch", and `--force` overrides. `own-stack` (the 7 glass cases): refused while a stack's `ports.json` is in `VERIFY_RUN_DIR`, also with `--force`.
- The optional-seed exemption in the self-test covers only a seed the usage names inside "(optional …)", not the whole case.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the self-test after "Spec parse gate (#1052)" and before "Install Playwright chromium", so the spec-parse comment's "first signal after install" holds again.
- Four probe headers say `vp.mjs archive` instead of `cp`; spec 28 §4 P1 says `archive` copies and `links` prints the raw links after the push, and §8 records P0 and P1. `docs/verify/1402/README.md` indexes every evidence directory of both segments with its round, commit and leg.
- `SKILL.md`, `features/README.md`, the Cursor flow step 4 and the changelog (`2026-10-20-1402.md`, segment 2 section) describe the marks and the gate.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([seg2-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-failure-modes.txt)). The self-test cases on `c3f22bc` (tests only) against main's `vp.mjs` and registry read 54/66: 12 of the 13 new cases fail, and the `VERIFY_WEB_PORT` pin passes because main already refuses a mismatched web port. At `87480f0` and `2ddff26` they read 66/66 on Node 22 and Node 24 ([seg2-selftest.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-selftest.txt)).

Live, using only `vp.mjs --help` and the maps' drive lines on a fresh stack at 8791 / 5273 ([seg2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-live.txt)):

- `api-keys create` 6/6, `search search` 2/2 and `theme persist` 2/2 pass.
- On the same stack a second `api-keys create` and `glass-journeys create-task` (also with `--force`) exit 2 with their reasons; after `cleanup`, `create-task` passes 3/3 on its own stack.
- The runs were archived with `vp.mjs archive 1402 --from …` into four directories; repeating an archive is refused; `vp.mjs links 1402` printed the links after the commit.
- pr-gate run 9's add-only case, replayed with `--dry-run` from a sibling worktree: main's `vp.mjs` targets that worktree's archived directory (exit 0), this branch's refuses it (exit 2).

The negative control (ticket acceptance 3) is segment 1's; the README links it.

27 mutations, each run in a scratch copy, are each caught ([seg2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-mutations.txt)). The first pass caught 26: reading the worktree list only from `vp.mjs`'s repository passed because the test's caller and `vp.mjs` shared one repository. `668e79c` adds a second clone as the caller, and that mutation is red.

Gates at `87480f0` and `2ddff26` ([gates-seg2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/gates-seg2.txt)): `pnpm lint` (the existing info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the self-test, the feature-map staleness gate (334 references, baseline unchanged), the registry gate, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (no file selected) and `e2e:affected` (no web surface) exit 0. `/code-review` at low effort, run twice, and `/simplify` (a shared worktree helper in the self-test, a derived support list, duplicate roots skipped before git runs) are in [seg2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-reviews.txt); neither review read the self-test's own hunks, which the mutations cover.

## Upstream

No dependency. The gate uses only Node's standard library; `git worktree list --porcelain` gives the worktree roots.

## Risk

Two-way door. A new `drive-<number>.mjs` now fails CI even when registered; a probe is named for its feature. If main gains another `drive-<number>` script before this merges, the gate fails until that script is renamed or added to the frozen list. A fresh-stack case can need `cleanup` and `launch` between drives where it used to run and fail; `--force` keeps the old behavior. `vp.mjs` runs `git worktree list` only when an evidence directory has to be checked.

`03-keys-once.png` in the new `api-keys` run shows the one-time plaintext of a key minted on a scratch stack that `vp.mjs cleanup` deleted; it authenticates nothing, as in segment 1.

The patch is 2,226 lines (898 outside `docs/verify/`) across 70 files and touches `.claude/**`, `.cursor/**`, `.github/**` and `docs/spec/**`, so under ADR 0021 D4 it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] `vp.mjs --help` lists every subcommand (segment 1; `seg2-live.txt`)
- [x] Three existing features driven end to end from `--help` and the feature maps alone, and archived (`seg2-live.txt`)
- [x] Negative control: a seeded regression turns `drive` red (segment 1, linked from `README.md`)
- [x] A new `drive-<number>` script turns the static gate red; existing scripts stay green (`seg2-selftest.txt`, `seg2-mutations.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / e2e:affected pass (`gates-seg2.txt`)
- [x] pr-gate run 9's segment 2 list: worktree guard, CI order, probe headers, README index, pins, stack-state marks (`seg2-selftest.txt`, `seg2-live.txt`)

## Issues

Segment 2 of 2 for #1402; the squash message below carries its closing line.

Squash with this message:

```
verify(1402): registry gate, drive lines in the feature maps, stack-state marks (#1476)

scripts/vp-registry-gate.mjs fails CI on an unregistered script, a new
drive-<number> script, an empty registry, a missing path, an unknown
status or need, a docs/verify writes path without rewrites-evidence,
or a feature map whose drive lines do not match the registry. The 35
feature maps with a recipe name their vp.mjs drive commands. vp.mjs
refuses evidence directories in the docs/verify of every git worktree,
and drive checks two registry marks: fresh-stack cases need a stack
with no recorded drive, own-stack cases need no stack up. The CI
self-test runs after the spec-parse gate. docs/verify/1402/README.md
indexes the evidence of both segments.

closes #1402

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012odUHNQRa4CWjzR22iWH8s

mergedPulls.title: server(1404): merge gate S3, gate tables migration
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment S3 of #1404 (bootstrap phase P3, the merge-readiness gate; plan in https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1404#issuecomment-6304303150). One migration, `apps/server/drizzle/0044_merge_gate_tables.sql`, adds the four server-owned tables the later segments write and read. Nothing writes to them yet.

- `gate_digest`, primary key (`buildId`, `headSha`): the patch digest S1 computes for a build's PR at one head (`patchDigest`, the counted and kept file and line totals the D4 size caps use). A new head after update-branch gets its own row.
- `gate_round`, one row per review round, UNIQUE (`buildId`, `patchDigest`) and UNIQUE (`buildId`, `round`): the round number, which `[review-fix]` round produced the patch, the frozen perspectives, the perspectives that timed out, dispatch counts per kind and perspective with the last dispatch time, and the round state (`open`, `fixing`, `fix_no_change`, `closed`). These are the fields S2's readiness reads and S7 will coordinate.
- `gate_verdict`, primary key `stepId` (no foreign key to `step`), indexed by `buildId`: kind, perspective, outcome and `patchDigest` as S2's `GateVerdictView` carries them (a null digest counts toward no patch), the head the step reported and the head the server pinned at dispatch (`expectedHeadSha`, not null). `stepId` has no foreign key, as `plan`, `steer_pending` and `stop_pending` have none: drizzle runs migrations inside a transaction, where `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` has no effect, so a cascade from `step` would delete every verdict whenever a later migration recreates `step`, and a step deleted without its build would take a recorded block with it. Verdicts live here and not in message rows, because the machine transcript upload accepts any role and id (plan fact 1); nothing on the machine upload path refers to these tables.
- `gate_state`, primary key `buildId`: the latest readiness snapshot (ready, head, digest, policy, blockers as JSON).
- Every `buildId` is a foreign key to `build` with on-delete cascade, as `plan` and `branch_sync` have. The tables are registered in `DB_TABLES` and `INTERNAL_ONLY_TABLES` (`packages/shared/src/tables.ts`). Column comments in `schema.ts` name the S1 or S2 type each column holds; the value lists are `$type` literals without CHECK constraints, as elsewhere in the schema.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([s3-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-failure-modes.txt)). The new tests against main's schema fail 22 of 141 (19 of the 20 new tests plus the table registry, vocabulary and snapshot tests); on the branch 141 of 141 pass ([s3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-red-green.txt)). The one new test that passes on main checks that the machine upload code does not refer to the gate tables, which holds before and after. The tests find the migration by content, not number, and check that its journal `when` is later than every earlier entry, since drizzle skips a migration whose `when` is not newer than the last one applied.

Live ([s3-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-live.txt), servers on 8795 and 8796 with scratch homes, read with better-sqlite3):

- Main's server (`2294b08`) made a database with 44 migrations, 31 tables and a project, task and build; this branch's server then started on the same home and applied 0044 (45 migrations, 35 tables), the build row intact, and gate rows could be written for it.
- A second (`buildId`, `patchDigest`) or (`buildId`, `round`) fails on the unique index; a second `stepId`, `gate_state` or `gate_digest` row fails on the primary key; a verdict for a missing step failed on the foreign key. That last claim is round 1 only: round 2 removed the `stepId` foreign key (commit 2136fea), F5 at the head asserts that such a verdict is stored, and the live evidence for the head is [s3-r2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-live.txt).
- `DELETE /api/todos/:id` (204), `POST /api/todos/:id/reset` (200, the other build's rows untouched) and `DELETE /api/projects/:id` (204) each leave no gate rows for the removed builds. At the head, `s3-r2-live.txt` covers `DELETE /api/todos/:id` live; reset and project delete at the head rest on the F7 tests.

Round 1: eight mutations, each with the migration regenerated by drizzle-kit, are each caught ([s3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-mutations.txt)): either unique index removed, `patchDigest` not null, no cascade on the verdict's build or step, no foreign key on `gate_state`, the step foreign key dropped, the journal `when` set below 0043's. Two of these (no cascade on the verdict's step, the step foreign key dropped) concern the `stepId` foreign key that round 2 removed, so they no longer apply to the head; the step foreign key dropped is now the shipped schema.

Gates ([gates-s3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/gates-s3.txt)): `pnpm lint` (the existing info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), the warning cap, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate, `db:check`, `db:generate` with no new migration, the feature-map staleness gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2456 with the one root-only failure (`runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败": `chmodSync(cwd, 0o500)` does nothing for root; CI runs as a normal user). `/code-review` at low effort on `origin/main..claude/bootstrap-p3c` found nothing.

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 (go at `3330010`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1469-run1-3330010.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1469-run1-3330010.json)), at `4d37bfe` ([s3-r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-red-green.txt), [s3-r2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-mutations.txt), [s3-r2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-live.txt), [s3-r2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-reviews.txt), [gates-s3-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/gates-s3-2.txt)). The run showed that the `stepId` foreign key with cascade would let a drizzle-shaped recreate of `step` wipe every verdict; it is gone, and 0044 is regenerated with only that line removed. New tests: a recreate of `step` after the gate migration keeps every verdict (F17); a step deleted without its build keeps its verdict (F18); every migration after the gate migration keeps the gate rows (F19, with mutations that recreate `build` or `todo` showing it red); null `expectedHeadSha` and null round digest are refused (F20, F21). The upgrade test seeds the old database with SQL instead of the head's `seed()`. Red 3 of 146 on `f859a18` (tests only), green 146 of 146; 12 mutations that go red plus 2 controls that stay green (one moves gate rows aside around a `build` recreate, the other recreates `step`). Live, main's server made a database, this branch's server upgraded it: `gate_verdict` has one foreign key (`buildId`), a verdict on a missing step is stored, deleting the step keeps it, and deleting the task clears all four tables (that live run covers `DELETE /api/todos/:id`; reset and project delete rest on the F7 tests). `/simplify` folded the table counts into one query; `/code-review` at medium effort on the branch's three-dot diff, test file included, raised 9 points: one comment fixed, the rest kept with their reasons in `s3-r2-reviews.txt`. Gates at `34381bd`: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate, `db:check`, `db:generate` with no change and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` had the root-only runner-brief case and one `skill-write` timeout under a load of 24 on 4 CPUs, which passes 30 of 30 alone. `4d37bfe` changes one schema comment.

pr-gate run 2 at `4d37bfe` returned go with 0 blocking and 8 suggestions, all handled in this body (Verified, Risk, Issues and Acceptance); the dispositions are in a comment on this PR, and the verdict JSON is kept in the session scratchpad, not committed.

## Upstream

No dependency. drizzle-kit generates the migration, journal entry and snapshot with the repo's `db:generate`; `db:check` passes.

## Risk

Two-way door at the code level, one-way for a database that ran it: SQLite keeps the tables after a revert, and a later 0044 from another branch would collide with this number. CLAUDE.md numbers migrations at merge time, so if main gains a 0044 first this branch regenerates its migration under the next number; the tests do not depend on the number.

The columns are the plan's plus a few later segments will need (`gate_verdict.headSha`, `gate_round`'s second unique index, `fixRound`, `perspectives`, `timedOut`, `dispatches`); the round `state` list is a proposal for S7. S1 writes digests as `pd2:<hex>` now; the column is plain text. `keptLines` is the sum of additions and deletions over S1's kept files, since S1 exposes no such total. A step dispatched without a pinned head gets no verdict row (`expectedHeadSha` is not null). A later migration that recreates `build`, or `todo` (which cascades into `build`), must move the gate rows aside and back, as the schema comment and F19 say; making `migrate` run with foreign keys off is a separate change to `db/client.ts`; where S5a stores the pinned head at dispatch is S5a's choice. The table list in spec 01 §6 is historical and already misses several tables, so it is not edited; `DB_TABLES` is the maintained list.

Kept unfixed from the round-2 `/code-review` (reasons in [s3-r2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-reviews.txt)):

- Point 7: F15 is a text check over `routes-machine.ts` and `services/machine*.ts`, so it also passes on main; the behavioural guard comes with S5a's writer.
- Point 8: `memory()` in the test never closes its handle and runs the 45 migrations per test; in-memory handles are released when the vitest worker for the file exits, the test needs the raw handle that `openDbWithHandle` does not return, and a fresh database per test is the isolation the tests use.
- Point 9: F7 calls `s.dispose()` after its assertions, not in `finally`; the rest of `apps/server/test` does the same (432 call sites) and each test boots its own in-memory server, so a failed assertion cannot leak state into another test's database.

Test limits at this head: F19 runs no later migration (0044 is the last journal entry), and the kind and outcome test copies S2's value lists by hand, so both bite only when a later migration is added or S2's lists change; S5a and later segments carry behavioural tests.

The schema comment at `apps/server/src/db/schema.ts` lines 769-772 and 787-788 names S2's `readiness.ts` and `MERGE_BLOCKERS` / `BLOCKER_CLASSES` / `mergeBlockerSchema`, which land with #1421; until #1421 merges those names are not on main.

mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment S2 of #1404 (bootstrap phase P3, the merge readiness gate), on top of S1 (#1420, on main as `9eefe88`). The segment plan is in the ticket comment (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1404#issuecomment-6304303150). This segment adds the blocker vocabulary and one pure function, `mergeReadiness`. Nothing calls it yet; S6a wires it in as an observer.

- `packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts` gains `MERGE_BLOCKERS`: 50 codes in a fixed order, each with a class (`policy`, `transient` or `human`) and a Chinese label, plus `mergeBlockerSchema` and `mergeReadinessSchema` (`ready`, `headSha`, `patchDigest`, `policy`, `blockers`). The order is the order the status description and the detail page will show.
- `apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/readiness.ts` has `mergeReadiness(inputs)`. The inputs are facts the I/O shell reads (S4/S5): policy and pause, the build lane, the PR, checks on the current head (with a flag that the lists were read in full), the compare (its files and this PR's commits), verdicts with the digest each one is bound to, the round, and which perspectives, verifier and decider the team has. It reads no database, sends no request and takes no clock. The rules from the design:
  - an input it cannot read is a transient blocker, not a skip (`pr-unreadable`, also for a default branch it cannot read; `required-checks-unreadable`; `patch-unavailable` when the compare cannot be read; `mergeable-state` while GitHub is still computing; a check list not read in full counts as unreadable, since a missing check may sit on the page not read); a patch it read but cannot bind waits for a person instead (`compare-truncated`, `compare-malformed` when the compare response has the wrong shape, and `patch-unbindable` when only evidence changed or a file has no blob sha);
  - every blocker is listed, sorted by the vocabulary, so the same inputs give the same first blocker;
  - verdicts count only at the current patch digest; a verdict on an old digest or not bound to a head counts as missing; a later pass at the same digest clears an earlier extraction failure or invalid evidence; a tampered verdict on any digest of the build blocks until a new build, since a new patch does not undo a tamper;
  - a blocking review blocks even when chief said go, and a later pass from the same perspective does not clear it;
  - a missing required check blocks (ci-loop treats it as a grace period, the gate does not); a required check can come from a check run or a commit status; `neutral` and `skipped` pass a required check as branch protection does, while `pr-evidence` must be `success`;
  - any non-passing check other than the gate's own `pacman/merge-gate` status blocks (`mergeable-state`) even when GitHub still reports `clean` or `has_hooks`, because the function's own check list is read later than GitHub computes the state; `unstable` passes only when at least one non-passing check is visible and all of them are the gate's own status, so the gate does not block on itself; `pacman/merge-gate` set as a required check is its own blocker;
  - size cap 800 lines or 40 files over the whole patch, evidence included (ADR 0021 D4 as amended on #1410), from S1's counts; the D4 path classes from S1's `classifyPaths`, including `opaque-file` for a file outside `docs/verify/` that GitHub sent without a patch (a binary file, a very large diff or a pure rename); a raw evidence link counts only when its sha is one of this PR's commits (from the same compare response) and its path is a file this PR adds or changes under this ticket's directory; without a compare the link check is skipped, because the compare blocker already stops the merge.

## Verified

Old leg: the test file before `readiness.ts` existed ([s2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/s2-red-green.txt)):

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts
 FAIL  |@xiechimon/pacman| test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts
Error: Cannot find module '../src/services/merge-gate/readiness.js'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

New leg at `97a1f76`:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  68 passed (68)
```

The tests start from one all-green input and flip one fact per row, one row for each of the 47 codes; a completeness test fails when a code has no row. Further tests cover the combinations the design names: chief go next to a blocking review, a pass after a block, verdicts on an old or unbound digest, the gate's own status making the PR unstable, a foreign check doing so, a required check from a commit status, `neutral` on `pr-evidence`, unknown ancestry, the frozen round perspectives, ordering, and the 800 / 40 boundaries.

Mutation round 1 ran 19 mutations of `readiness.ts`; two survived ([s2-mutations-1.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-1.txt)): treating a null `mergeable_state` like any other non-clean state, and counting a failed verify step as a verdict. One test was added and one tightened; round 2 catches 19 of 19 ([s2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations.txt), definitions at the end of the file):

```
