verdicts on any digest count                  1 failed | 67 passed (68)
own status unstable blocks                    1 failed | 67 passed (68)
missing required check is green               1 failed | 67 passed (68)
unknown ancestry counts                       1 failed | 67 passed (68)
mergeable null accepted                       1 failed | 67 passed (68)
failed verify step counts as a verdict        1 failed | 67 passed (68)
...
```

Gates ([gates-s2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2.txt)): `pnpm lint` (790 files, the existing `noUselessFragments` info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), `scripts/lint-warning-cap.mjs` (0 warnings), `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm spec:parse` pass; `pnpm --filter @pacman/web e2e:affected` ran `token-gate.spec.ts`, 6 passed. `pnpm exec vitest run --changed` ran 242 files: 2518 passed and one failed, the same root-only `runner-brief.test.ts` case as in S1 (`chmodSync(cwd, 0o500)` does nothing for root; CI runs as a normal user).

S1's round 2 (#1420 at `11ecbde`, after its pr-gate run 1) came into this branch by a merge commit at `4228232`; nothing in `readiness.ts` changed with it. On that head the four merge-gate test files pass 137 of 137 (69 from S1, 68 from S2), and CI was green.

Round 2, after the `/code-review` pass on this PR, at `13c0171` ([s2-r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a13169be1fdb1e9ddd843f566b58f93745d734b6/docs/verify/1404/s2-r2-red-green.txt), [s2-mutations-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a13169be1fdb1e9ddd843f566b58f93745d734b6/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-2.txt), [gates-s2-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/a13169be1fdb1e9ddd843f566b58f93745d734b6/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-2.txt)). The review found that an unbindable digest was a transient blocker the gate would wait on for good, that a failing check outside the required set passed while GitHub still said `clean` and `unstable` passed with nothing failing in view, that a later pass never cleared invalid evidence, and that an unreadable default branch went to a person. The new tests read 9 failed of 80 against `333d4f5` and 80 of 80 at `13c0171`; 16 of 16 mutations are caught.

Round 3, after the ADR 0021 D4 amendment on #1410 and S1's round 3 (#1420 at `0cc6b16`, merged in at `5070956` without conflicts), at `df417c8` ([s2-r3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ee11f2060bbe67499261605054dbd63fedb74de9/docs/verify/1404/s2-r3-red-green.txt), [s2-mutations-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ee11f2060bbe67499261605054dbd63fedb74de9/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-3.txt), [gates-s2-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ee11f2060bbe67499261605054dbd63fedb74de9/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-3.txt)). `opaque-file` is new; the caps already read S1's counts, so the tests that put evidence over 40 files or 800 lines pass on both sides and the mutations that count only `digest.kept` hold them. Red 4 failed of 163 (readiness plus the three S1 files), green 163 of 163; 7 of 7 mutations caught. Gates for rounds 2 and 3: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, test-spawn-gate and e2e:affected pass; `vitest run --changed` has the same one root-only failure.

Round 4, after pr-gate's first run on this PR (go, suggestions only) and S1's round 5 (#1420 at `02780b4`, merged in at `7f4a1f8` without conflicts; the readiness fixtures moved from `hasPatch` to S1's `patchSha` in that merge), at `acdf494` and `b1eee22` ([s2-r4-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ccfd218b84da274b3dd1765d264ed4aa5bee00c7/docs/verify/1404/s2-r4-red-green.txt), [s2-mutations-4.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ccfd218b84da274b3dd1765d264ed4aa5bee00c7/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-4.txt), [gates-s2-4.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ccfd218b84da274b3dd1765d264ed4aa5bee00c7/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-4.txt)). The input contract changed: `compare` (`{files, commits}`, `'unreadable'` or `'malformed'`) replaces `compareFiles` and `evidenceLinkAncestry`, and `checks.complete` is new. A link at a commit that is an ancestor of the head but not part of this PR (a main commit), or at a file this PR does not add, no longer counts; a malformed compare goes to a person instead of waiting; a half-read check list is not judged. Readiness also counts a file without a patch under a case variant of `docs/verify/` (both names of a rename) as `opaque-file`, since the digest does not treat it as evidence. Because the old code reads the removed field, the red leg fails all 94 readiness tests (92 on a TypeError, 1 through `not.toThrow`, 1 on the completeness row), so it shows the contract break, not each rule; 11 of 11 mutations, one or more per rule, each turn a test red. Green 193 of 193 over the four merge-gate files, recorded at `acdf494`; the `/simplify` commit `b1eee22` was checked with lint, typecheck and the four files, and that run is not archived. Gates at `acdf494`: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, test-spawn-gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed` has the one root-only failure (2618 passed). The `/simplify` commit `b1eee22` folds the digest checks into one guarded block and uses `EVIDENCE_PREFIX`; lint, typecheck and the four merge-gate files pass there. The `/code-review` pass on the round found only the case-sensitive check-run match already listed under Risk.

Round 5, after S1's rounds 6 and 7 (#1420 at `1892662`, merged in at `375c9ab` without conflicts; the four merge-gate files passed 216 of 216 on the merge), at `8240d4b` ([s2-r5-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/63051007fd362bf632692ce0fd894fe61e67c086/docs/verify/1404/s2-r5-red-green.txt), [s2-mutations-5.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/63051007fd362bf632692ce0fd894fe61e67c086/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-5.txt), [gates-s2-5.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/63051007fd362bf632692ce0fd894fe61e67c086/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-5.txt)). S1's `classifyPaths` now matches the evidence prefix with case for its `opaque` exemption, so the readiness supplement for case variants of `docs/verify/` is removed and readiness blocks on `paths.opaque` alone; the readiness test that pins case variants is unchanged and passes through S1. With S1's exemption turned back to ignoring case, that readiness test fails (2 failed of 216, the other being S1's own paths test), while the same revert against the round 4 readiness stays green, so readiness now depends on S1 for the rule. Every S2 mutation of rounds 1 to 4 that still applies was re-run against the round 5 readiness, 51 of 51 caught, which includes 2 new ones on S1's exemption and 3 adapted to reworded text; 7 no longer apply because their text is gone. Green 216 of 216 at `8240d4b`. Gates: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed` has the one root-only failure (2641 passed). `/code-review` on the round found nothing.

After round 5 the branch took S1's round 8 (#1420 at `92bd34b`, which carries main with #1410) by a merge commit at `4ae9bb5`, without conflicts; readiness and its tests needed no change, the four merge-gate files pass 228 of 228, and the gates exit 0 except the root-only runner-brief case ([s2-r6-merge.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/68d499f429b375d397bf35b27f0174b83db3718f/docs/verify/1404/s2-r6-merge.txt)).

Round 7, after pr-gate run 2 on this PR (go at `68d499f`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1421-run2-68d499f.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/04ffa3bef2bedc4f110e9d0d3c03cb89cb53fd59/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1421-run2-68d499f.json)), at `17474b1` ([s2-r7-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/04ffa3bef2bedc4f110e9d0d3c03cb89cb53fd59/docs/verify/1404/s2-r7-red-green.txt), [s2-mutations-7.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/04ffa3bef2bedc4f110e9d0d3c03cb89cb53fd59/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-7.txt), [gates-s2-7.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/04ffa3bef2bedc4f110e9d0d3c03cb89cb53fd59/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-7.txt)). Names that the PR author or a third party chooses (file names in the path blockers, check names, required check names, branch names, the head repository) reach `detail` only as JSON strings, with C1 controls, format characters such as bidi overrides, and line and paragraph separators also written as `\uXXXX`; each name is cut at 120 escaped characters with `…` outside the quotes, and each list at 10 names plus `+N more`. A file name with a newline and instruction-like text becomes one quoted line that parses back to the name. The run's other suggestions are now pinned, each red under its own mutation: a later pass clears an extraction failure for verify, review and the chief decision; `dirty`, `blocked`, `behind`, `draft` and `unknown` each give only `mergeable-state`; a 300-file compare gives `compare-truncated`; `Pacman/merge-gate` in mixed case counts as the gate's own status and own required name; the fork compare ignores case; the `merged` flag is honored; a deleted head repository gives `pr-from-fork`. Red 7 of 114 readiness tests against `68d499f` (the five new detail tests and two whose expected detail now carries quoted names; the pins pass there too), green 248 of 248 over the four merge-gate files. Every S2 mutation that still applies was re-run with the 23 new ones: 74 applied, 74 caught, 10 no longer apply. Gates: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed` has the one root-only failure (2673 passed). `/code-review` on the round found nothing.

Round 8, after pr-gate run 3 (go at `04ffa3b`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1421-run3-04ffa3b.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1421-run3-04ffa3b.json)) and #1420's merge, at `4cd4502` ([s2-r8-merge.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36/docs/verify/1404/s2-r8-merge.txt), [s2-r8-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36/docs/verify/1404/s2-r8-red-green.txt), [s2-mutations-8.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-8.txt), [gates-s2-8.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-8.txt), [s2-r8-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36/docs/verify/1404/s2-r8-reviews.txt)). The branch took main at `49af6f2` by a merge commit (`a570f79`). The one conflict was `packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts`, where main has S1's 161 lines and this branch has the same lines plus S2's vocabulary; the other 38 S1 files match main exactly, and the base is now main. Readiness blocks with `patch-unavailable` ("compare not read at the PR head") when `compare.commits` does not contain `pr.headSha`, and then treats the compare as unread, so it never reports a head as ready from inputs read at another one. The `verify-missing` detail counts only verdicts on another digest or with none and names failed verify steps separately. The input contract says S4 keeps one check run per app and name. New pins: a blocking review, verify or chief decision on an earlier digest next to passes on the current one gives no blocker; `{pass, null}` for each kind and `{tampered, null}` alone; a table maps every one of the 50 codes to its class; two same-named check runs from two apps are both counted. The test files state their failure modes as current rules. Red 2 of 259 on `2cf49a9` (tests only), green 259 of 259 (readiness 125). Every earlier S2 mutation that still applies and 63 new ones (13 rules and pins, plus a class flip for each code) give 137 of 137 caught. Gates at `4cd4502`: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` has the one root-only failure (2727 passed). `/code-review` on the round found nothing.

## Upstream

No dependency decides merge readiness from these inputs. The GitHub facts come from the docs. The protected-branches page says required status checks "can be checks or commit statuses" and "must have a `successful`, `skipped`, or `neutral` status". The GraphQL `MergeStateStatus` enum lists `BEHIND`, `BLOCKED`, `CLEAN`, `DIRTY`, `DRAFT`, `HAS_HOOKS` ("Mergeable with passing commit status and pre-receive hooks"), `UNKNOWN` ("cannot currently be determined") and `UNSTABLE` ("Mergeable with non-passing commit status"); REST's `mergeable_state` carries the same names in lower case, as reads of #1410, #1411 and #1420 show (`unstable`, `clean`, `blocked`). The function treats a null state like `unknown`.

## Risk

Two-way door. New code with no caller, so no running behaviour changes. `packages/shared` gains exports only; `pnpm typecheck` covers every consumer. The vocabulary is a contract for S5 to S9 (status description, chief tool, detail page); renaming a code later means touching those, which is why the order and codes are fixed now and tested for completeness. The 50 labels are Chinese and not yet in the i18n dictionaries; S9 moves them when the web reads them. Left from the `/code-review` pass: required check names match check runs with case and commit statuses without it; GitHub's branch protection sends a mismatch to `blocked` anyway, and the gate reads that state. The ticket's S2 also names a pure driver, `nextGateActions(facts)`; it moves to S4, which has the first facts to drive it. The compare response lists at most 250 commits per page, so the shell (S4) has to page through `commits`; a partial list can only make a link not count, which blocks. Readiness cannot tell whether a linked file exists at the linked commit (a link at an earlier commit of this PR to a file added later is a 404 that both rules accept), because compare gives no per-commit file lists; S4's shell checks the file at that sha, and a test pins that readiness leaves it. Against main the patch is 5,699 lines (1,864 outside `docs/verify/`) across 33 files; outside the evidence it is the merge gate's own source and test comments in S1's test files, ADR 0021 D4 class 4, so this PR waits for a user merge. GitHub's commit list for this PR now starts with S1's original commits, so the squash message must come from the block under Issues, not from the first commit's message.

## Acceptance

- [x] Blocker vocabulary in shared, one test row per code, completeness test (`merge-gate-readiness.test.ts`)
- [x] Unreadable inputs block as transient, unbindable patches go to a person; all blockers listed in vocabulary order
- [x] Verdicts only at the current digest; blocking review beats chief go; no re-roll after a block
- [x] Required checks: missing blocks, commit statuses count, `pr-evidence` only `success`; own status does not block, any other non-passing check does, whatever GitHub's state says
- [x] Whole-patch caps and files without a patch outside the evidence (`opaque-file`), case variants of the evidence prefix included
- [x] Compare read but malformed goes to a person; evidence links only at this PR's commits and files; incomplete check lists not judged (round 4)
- [x] Names in `detail` quoted, escaped and bounded; pr-gate run 2's untested rules pinned (round 7, `s2-r7-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Inputs read at another head never give ready; every code's class pinned (round 8, `s2-r8-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Mutations: 19 of 19 after two survivors in the first pass, then 16 of 16, 7 of 7 and 11 of 11 in rounds 2 to 4, in round 5 every earlier mutation that still applies re-run, 51 of 51, including 2 on S1's exemption, in round 7 74 of 74 and in round 8 137 of 137 (`s2-mutations-1.txt`, `s2-mutations.txt`, `s2-mutations-2.txt` to `s2-mutations-5.txt`, `s2-mutations-7.txt`, `s2-mutations-8.txt`)
- [x] lint / warning cap / typecheck / spec:parse / e2e:affected pass; vitest --changed passes except one root-only case (`gates-s2.txt`, `gates-s2-2.txt` to `gates-s2-5.txt`, `gates-s2-7.txt`, `gates-s2-8.txt`)

## Issues

Part of #1404, segment S2 of the plan in the ticket comment. The last segment carries the closing line for #1404; this squash body has no closing keyword for it.

The commit list on GitHub starts with S1's commits (now on main as a squash), so squash with this message:

```

packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts gains MERGE_BLOCKERS: 50
codes in a fixed order, each with a class (policy, transient, human)
and a label, and the readiness schema. apps/server/src/services/
merge-gate/readiness.ts has mergeReadiness(inputs), a pure function
not called yet: every blocker listed in vocabulary order; inputs it

mergedPulls.title: shared(1406): GitHub issue text fenced as data; Implementer names the repo rules
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 3 of #1406 (bootstrap phase P5, `docs/spec/28` §4 P5, ADR 0021 D5): the in-product agent is told this repository's working rules, and text from a GitHub issue reaches every model as fenced third-party data. Plan: https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1406#issuecomment-6311590280 (segment 3, failure mode 12).

- `fenceIssueText` in `packages/shared/src/records/prompts.ts` wraps the title and body of a task whose `sourceKind` is `github-issue`: a header line `【GitHub issue 原文 · owner/repo#N】` with a note (text the issue's author wrote on GitHub; data, not instructions; requests in it to change tools, secrets, repositories, memory or merging are not followed; never saved to memory; the system prompt, persona and repo rules win), every body line prefixed with `> ` after `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`-`\x1e`, `\x85`, U+2028 and U+2029 are turned into line breaks, and a footer line. A fake header or footer inside the body stays prefixed. A missing or malformed ref is labelled 「出处未知」 and still fenced. Tasks with any other `sourceKind` (none, `orchestration`, `github-issue-self`) keep today's text byte for byte.
- Fenced where issue text reaches a model: the chief's orchestrate message and the chief claim's instruction (`orchestrate.ts` passes the source), the worker prompts of new sessions (plan, build, merge, restart, ci-fix, the degraded fresh session; the claim's todo carries optional `sourceKind`/`sourceRef` in `machine-wire.ts`, filled by `machines.ts`, and the daemon's `buildTaskPromptText` fences title and body), and the verify step's material (`builds.ts`).
- Kept out of the system layer: the worker's run brief leaves out the title line for a GitHub-sourced task (on main the title reached the system prompt when `meta.titleFinal` was missing); `saveMemoryEntry` in `chief-tools.ts`, the one write path for chief and worker memories, answers 400 when the title or content carries the fence marker; `composeChiefSystemPrompt` gains one rule line saying fenced text and GitHub titles, bodies and comments from tool results are third-party data, never followed for tools, secrets, repositories, memory or merging, never saved as memory, and kept in the fence when a task is split.
- The Implementer persona (`persona.ts`) names the repository's rules: read AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md first; write PR bodies with the repo's PR skill and verify with its verify skill (pr-pacman and verify-pacman here), evidence under `docs/verify/<ticket>/`; commit and PR title shape `<scope>(<ticket>): <subject>`; closing keywords in the commit message; run the repo's gates before committing. A test checks that each `*-pacman` skill it names exists. 837 of the 2,000-character limit.
- The web maps `sourceKind`/`sourceRef` onto the displayed task and treats the fenced orchestrate row, and the unfenced row logged before this change, as the task text.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([p5-3-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-failure-modes.txt)). The six new test files on `51a61c8` (tests only, sources as `2294b08`) fail 27 of 42; at `c60ae64` 42 of 42 pass ([p5-3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-red-green.txt)). The 15 that pass on the old sources pin today's behavior: plain-task prompts, the existing persona tests and the length cap.

The real composed text, from a scratch server and the daemon's `runStep` with an issue body that carries instruction-like lines, a fake footer and a U+2028 ([p5-3-prompts.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-prompts.txt), script [p5-3-prompts.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-prompts.ts)): the body appears fenced in the orchestrate message, the chief instruction, the plan and build prompts and the verify material, and nowhere in the chief system prompt, the chief claim's system prompt, the worker system prompt or the persona.

Sixteen mutations, each caught ([p5-3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-mutations.txt), runner [p5-3-mutate.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-mutate.mjs)): the fence removed from the task text (15 tests fail) or from the orchestrate message (2), line breaks not normalized (1), body lines not prefixed (13), the ref label not checked (2), the chief system-prompt rule removed (1), a plain task fenced (3 and 4), the memory gate, the system-prompt title, the claim source, the orchestrate source, the verify material, the two web mappings and a persona naming a skill that does not exist.

Gates at `c60ae64` ([gates-p5-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5-3.txt)): `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse` and the spawn gate exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2516 with the root-only runner-brief case (which #1456 has since made safe as root; it passes on a trial merge with main). The web change runs the full e2e suite through `e2e:affected`: 1180 passed and one failed, `composer-inline-mention.spec.ts:671` waiting 5 s for a chip animation attribute, which passed 96 of 96 in three reruns on the same port. A trial merge with main at `dabef48` has no conflicts and passes typecheck, lint and 202 tests across 13 files. `/code-review` at low effort found nothing. `/security-review` (AGENTS.md lists `machines.ts`) found nothing at its threshold ([p5-3-security-review.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-security-review.txt)).

## Upstream

No dependency. The claim's todo gains two optional fields typed as plain strings, so an older daemon parses a newer claim and a future `sourceKind` does not break it; the wire snapshot records the two fields.

## Risk

Two-way door. A GitHub-sourced task's prompts change shape; other tasks are unchanged byte for byte. Text the model copies out of the fence is not fenced by code: the chief's wake prompts quote the task title, the chief's tool results (todos, todo, conversation) return titles and specs, and split children get their spec from the chief with `sourceKind` `orchestration`; the chief rule and the Implementer note cover these, so they rest on the model following its prompt. A paraphrase saved as memory without the marker passes the memory gate. Skill selection in `machines.ts` matches keywords on the raw text; it chooses catalog entries and puts no issue text into the brief. In the chief thread view, Markdown lazy continuation renders the footer line inside the quote; the text the model reads is not affected.

Seeding never overwrites a persona row that exists, so a team seeded before this change, the live instance included, keeps the old Implementer text until someone edits it; new teams get the new text.

The live check of the engine reading AGENTS.md in a daemon worktree, skills usable and gates running needs a long-lived host and a daemon with model credentials: 待宿主 (spec 28 §8).

`docs/verify/1406/p5-3-prompts.ts` and `p5-3-mutate.mjs` are the scripts that produced their outputs; nothing runs them. The patch is 2,429 lines (1,242 outside `docs/verify/`) across 26 files and touches `apps/server/src/services/machines.ts` (ADR 0021 D4 class ⑤), so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Issue text fenced in every path where it reaches a model in code, and absent from every system layer (`issue-fence.test.ts` in shared, server and daemon, `p5-3-prompts.txt`)
- [x] Tasks not from GitHub keep their prompts byte for byte (`issue-fence.test.ts`)
- [x] Implementer persona names the repo rules and only skills that exist (`persona.test.ts`, `persona-repo-rules.test.ts`)
- [x] 16 of 16 mutations caught (`p5-3-mutations.txt`)
- [x] `/security-review` run, no finding at its threshold (`p5-3-security-review.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case and one unrelated e2e timing case that passed on rerun (`gates-p5-3.txt`)

The engine reading AGENTS.md in a daemon worktree with a model is 待宿主.

## Issues

Part of #1406, segment 3. #1406 stays open for P5b (PR review comments into fix rounds, after P4); this squash body has no closing keyword for it.

Squash with this message:

```
shared(1406): GitHub issue text fenced as data; Implementer names the repo rules (#1475)

A task imported from a GitHub issue reaches every model with its title
and body inside a fence (fenceIssueText): a header naming the issue and
saying the text is third-party data, every body line quoted, line
separators normalized, and a footer. The orchestrate message, the chief
claim, new-session worker prompts and the verify material carry it;
the run brief, the chief system prompt and the persona carry no issue
text, the chief system prompt says how to treat fenced and GitHub tool
text, and memory refuses the fence marker. Other tasks keep their
prompts byte for byte. The Implementer persona points at AGENTS.md /
CLAUDE.md and names the PR and verify skills, the commit shape and the
gates.

Part of #1406 (segment 3).

mergedPulls.title: server(1466): GitHub repo refs refuse dot segments; chief and MCP check the project's team
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Ticket #1466: two gaps found by the security pass on #1467 (P5a-2 of #1406).

- `parseGithubRepoRef` in `packages/shared/src/records/project.ts` is the one place that checks and splits `owner/repo`. It keeps the existing character set and rejects `.` and `..` as owner or repo, the only names that change a URL path when they are put in one (`repos/../user/issues` resolves to `/user/issues`). `isGithubRepoRef` is its true/false form, so POST and PATCH `/api/projects`, chief `connect_repo`, the web forms and the daemon PR probe all refuse such a value. `...`, `.github` and `my.org/repo.js` stay valid.
- `parseGithubIssueSourceRef` (`packages/shared/src/records/todo.ts`) applies the same check (and with it the `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` character set the stored repo already had), so a stored `github:../user#3` is refused by the source-issue echo and the #452 title write-back.
- `githubRepoOfProject` in `apps/server/src/services/git.ts` is the one place the server splits a stored `project.githubRepo` for an API request. A stored value that fails the check counts as "not a GitHub project" and no request is sent: the issue list and import, the #452 issue creation and retry, the CI check-runs poller, the PR state probe, and the delivery step that decides whether a build waits for CI (such a build goes to review, as in a project without a GitHub repository).
- `requireProjectRow` in `chief-tools.ts` and `mcp-face.ts` takes the caller's team and filters on it, so another team's project id gives the same 404 as a missing one. Callers: chief `docs`, `create_todo`, `update_project`, `connect_repo`, `run_builds`, `watch_todos`; MCP `create_todo`. `run_builds` and `watch_todos` check every task and its project before they start or watch anything, so a call that names another team's project changes nothing. Chief and MCP `todos` always filter on the team (another team's `projectId` lists `[]`, as a missing id does), and `watch_todos` skips another team's task as it skips a missing one.

## Verified

The new tests against unchanged sources (origin/main `2294b08`), [red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/red.txt):

```
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
      Tests  47 failed | 13 passed (60)
```

Each red case fails for the reason it names: a request to `repos/../user/...` recorded by the fake GitHub, or a call on another team's project that succeeds. The daemon probe case was added while checking callers; mutation M1, which restores the old check exactly, turns it red. Green at `18ca807` (the file names no commit; the code at `e87699c` is the same) ([green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/green.txt)):

```
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  69 passed (69)
```

Eight mutations, one per rule, are each caught ([mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/mutations.txt), runner [mutate.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/mutate.mjs), sources checked byte-identical afterwards): the dot check (37 tests fail), the source-ref check (9), `githubRepoOfProject` (10), the chief and MCP team filters (5 and 1), chief and MCP `todos` (1 each) and `watch_todos` (1).

Live, on a scratch server at `07ab360` (port 8795, scratch `PACMAN_HOME`, every outbound connection logged by a proxy on 8796), 41 checks pass ([live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/live.txt)):

- POST `/api/projects` answers 400 for `../user`, `./x`, `owner/..`, `owner/.`, `../..` and `{owner: "..", repo: "user"}`, and PATCH local to github answers 400 for three of them, each with no connection to api.github.com. `my.org/repo.js`, `x/...` and `octo-org/.github` pass the check.
- With `../user`, `owner/..` and `./x` written into the database, the issue list and import answer 404 for each; for the `../user` project a new task starts no issue creation, the retry answers "project is not github-backed" and a `github:../user#1` source ref answers "source issue not found" (the other two values are covered for these paths by tests R3 and R4). The proxy log holds 6 connections, all from the control calls on valid repositories.
- Over `/api/mcp` with team A's key, `create_todo` on team B's project returns the same text as a missing id and adds nothing; `todos` with team B's `projectId` returns `[]`. Team B and the GitHub connection row were made in SQL, since one team is reachable through the API. `watch_todos` is a chief tool and is covered by `project-team-guard.test.ts`.

Gates at `18ca807` ([gates.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/gates.txt)): `pnpm lint` (788 files, the existing info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed, port 8389 free) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2493 with the one root-only failure (`runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败": `chmodSync(cwd, 0o500)` does nothing for root, CI runs as a normal user). `/code-review` at low effort on `origin/main..claude/bootstrap-p5c-1466` found nothing ([reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/reviews.txt)). `/security-review` (AGENTS.md lists `mcp-face.ts`) ran on `origin/HEAD...HEAD` at `07ab360` with its diff taken from this branch and found nothing at its confidence threshold ([security-review.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/security-review.txt)); `reviews.txt` records an earlier attempt whose context came from another checkout.

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 (go at `e87699c`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1468-run1-e87699c.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/pr-gate-1468-run1-e87699c.json)), at `ab18cc3` ([r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/r2-red-green.txt), [r2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/r2-mutations.txt), [gates-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/gates-2.txt)). The run found two orderings this change got wrong. Chief `run_builds` checked the project's team after `startBuilds`, so a team-A task pointing at a team-B project (rows the earlier `create_todo` could make) started a build and then answered 404; `watch_todos` could watch earlier ids before the 404. Both now check every task first. The delivery step still read the raw `githubRepo` column, so a build delivered in a project with an invalid stored repo waited for a CI poller that now skips it; it uses `githubRepoOfProject` and goes to review. With the round 2 tests on `ddb06ca` (tests only, sources as `e87699c`) 6 of 41 fail; at `ab18cc3` 41 of 41 pass, and the wider suite passes (the run at this round was not archived; `r3-green.txt` records it at round 3). Four mutations (the project check back after `startBuilds`, checked one task at a time, the old `watch_todos` loop, the raw column) are each caught. The daemon probe test no longer asserts `https://github.com/../user.git`, which URL parsing turns into one segment on main too. Gates at `ab18cc3`: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2498 with the one root-only failure. `/code-review` on `e87699c..0a4b003` found nothing (its output was not kept; `r3-reviews.txt` reconstructs the call).

Round 3, after pr-gate run 2 (go at `0a4b003`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1468-run2-0a4b003.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/pr-gate-1468-run2-0a4b003.json)), at `193e664` ([r3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/r3-mutations.txt), [r3-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/r3-reviews.txt), [r3-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/r3-green.txt), [gates-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/gates-3.txt), [gates-3b.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/gates-3b.txt)). Round 2 moved R7 through `completeStep`, so the CI poller's guard for an invalid stored repo was no longer reached; R7b puts a delivered build straight into building for `../user` and `owner/..` and asserts no outbound call and one skipped candidate, and reverting the guard to main's form fails exactly those two cases. `/simplify` added one test helper (`mcpError`); the other points it raised are recorded with the reason they stay. The branch then took main at `49af6f2` (#1467) by a merge commit without conflicts, and `github-reads.ts` now gets owner and repo from `githubRepoOfProject` instead of its own split and dot check, with the same 404 and 409 answers; its bad-slug test now lists `./x`, `x/.` and `x/..`, and removing the shared dot check fails it. The wider set (the #1466 tests, github-reads, chief-dispatch, chief-watch, chief-tools, ci-loop and m4a-chief-loop) passes 165 of 165. Gates after the merge: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2677 with the one root-only failure. `/code-review` at low effort on the round found nothing; at that effort it read no test hunks, which the mutation runs cover.

## Upstream

No dependency. The naming rule comes from GitHub's docs ("Creating a new repository": letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`, at most 100 characters) and the WHATWG URL Standard (only `.`, `..` and their `%2e` forms are dot segments; `%` is outside the allowed characters). The sources are cited in `github-repo-ref.test.ts` and in the `project.ts` comment.

## Risk

Two-way door. A project whose stored `githubRepo` is `.` or `..` in either half now behaves as a project without a GitHub repository for every API read and write; such a value can no longer be stored. Same-team behavior of the chief and MCP tools is unchanged, except that chief `run_builds` with a list now refuses the whole list when one task is missing or belongs to another team's project, where before the earlier tasks were started; a call naming another team's project now gets 404 or `[]`, which matters only where a server holds more than one team.

Left as they are, recorded in `reviews.txt` and `security-review.txt`: clone URLs (`projectRepoRef`, `toProjectRecord`, the branch sync in `routes-builds.ts`) are still built from a stored invalid row; the host is fixed to github.com and the clone fails, and treating the row as unbound there would change what claimed steps receive. A task that was already stuck in building in such a project before this change stays there until a person moves it. MCP `run_builds` and the chief and MCP `schedule_todo` check the task's team but not its project's, as chief `run_builds` did before this change; chief and MCP `conversation`, chief `usage` and `save_memory` take no team check. They predate this change, reach no other team on a single-team server, and are #1470.

`docs/verify/1466/mutate.mjs` and `r2-mutate.mjs` are the mutation runners kept with their output; nothing runs them. The chief and MCP `todos` tools now filter on the team, which the ticket did not list; it only narrows what another team can read. #1467 is on main and its reads now go through `githubRepoOfProject` here. #1461 (issue intake) and #1414 (`githubTarget` in `ci-loop.ts`) still split `githubRepo` on their own; whichever of them merges after this PR routes through `githubRepoOfProject` in its merge. This branch and #1414 both change the check-runs poller in `apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts`, and `git merge-tree` reports a conflict there; whichever merges second takes main by a merge commit and keeps both changes. It merges cleanly with #1411, #1421, #1461 and #1467.

The patch is 3,838 lines (1,035 outside `docs/verify/`) across 36 files and touches `apps/server/src/services/mcp-face.ts` (ADR 0021 D4 class ⑤), so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] `.` and `..` refused as owner or repo on every write path, and a stored one sends no GitHub request (`red.txt`, `green.txt`, `live.txt`)
- [x] `requireProjectRow` filters on the caller's team in chief and MCP; another team's project answers as a missing one (`project-team-guard.test.ts`, `live.txt`)
- [x] 8 of 8 mutations caught, 4 of 4 in round 2 and the CI poller guard in round 3 (`mutations.txt`, `r2-mutations.txt`, `r3-mutations.txt`)
- [x] `github-reads.ts` (#1467) uses `githubRepoOfProject` after the merge of main (`gates-3b.txt`)
- [x] `run_builds` and `watch_todos` refuse before changing anything; a delivery in a project with an invalid stored repo goes to review (`r2-red-green.txt`)
- [x] `/security-review` run, no finding at its threshold (`security-review.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case (`gates.txt`, `gates-2.txt`, `gates-3.txt`, `gates-3b.txt`)

## Issues

The squash message below carries the closing line for #1466. The gaps were found by the security pass on #1467 (part of #1406).

Squash with this message:

```

. and .. as owner or repo; isGithubRepoRef and parseGithubIssueSourceRef
use it. The server splits a stored project.githubRepo only through
githubRepoOfProject, so an invalid stored value sends no GitHub request
(issue list and import, #452 issue creation and retry, CI check-runs,
PR state probe, delivery waiting for CI). requireProjectRow in
chief-tools and mcp-face filters on the caller's team; run_builds and
watch_todos check every task's project before changing anything; chief
and MCP todos always filter on the team. The GitHub read tools take
owner and repo from githubRepoOfProject.

closes #1466

mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 2 of 3 for #1406 (bootstrap phase P5a, `docs/spec/28`): the chief and MCP tools `issues`, `pull_requests` and `workflow_runs` read GitHub instead of returning empty stubs. The plan is in the ticket comment (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1406#issuecomment-6311590280).

- `apps/server/src/services/github-reads.ts` is the one implementation both faces call (`executeGithubReadTool(deps, teamId, name, params)`), the way `listTodos` is shared. Nothing reaches GitHub until the project passes a gate: it is looked up by id and the caller's team (another team's project gives the same 404 as a missing one), `repoKind` must be `github`, and `githubRepo` must be a well-formed `owner/repo` without a `.` or `..` segment. The team's token comes from `openGithubToken`; no connection gives 404 and a token that will not decrypt gives 409 asking to reconnect. There is no anonymous fallback.
- `issues`: open, closed or all (default open), page and per page (at most 30), pull requests filtered out, no bodies; each entry carries number, title, state, labels, author, author association, times, a URL built from the slug and number, and `taskId`, the id of this team's task made from that issue (matched without case) or null. `pull_requests`: state, page and per page (at most 30), with draft, merged time, head and base refs and author, no bodies. `workflow_runs`: optional branch and status (one of GitHub's 14 documented values, checked locally because GitHub answers 200 with no runs for an unknown one), at most 20, with `exclude_pull_requests=true`.
- GitHub text is data: titles are cut to 200 code points and other strings to 100, format characters (bidi overrides, zero-width, tag characters) are removed, runs of control and separator characters become one space, and the tool descriptions say these fields are written by third parties.
- Failures come back as short `github: ...` errors without URL or token: 401, 403 and 422 as 424, 404 as 404, rate limits (any 429, or a 403 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `retry-after`, or a rate-limit body) as 429, GitHub 5xx, network errors and malformed responses as 502, and a timeout as 504. Each read times out at 6 s, under the 10 s relay timeout.
- `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts` gains `githubListIssues`, `githubListPulls` and `githubListWorkflowRuns` right after `githubRepoIssue`, away from the regions #1414 and #1461 change; `git merge-tree` against both, and against both together, is clean.
- `packages/shared/src/protocol/chief-tools.ts`: one zod schema per tool, used by both faces; MCP's `projectId` is now required, as it is on chief. The chief parameter schema uses only `type` and `description`, because the daemon's claude-code converter refuses `enum`, `integer` or `minimum` for the whole chief tool set and daemons already installed do not upgrade with the server; the allowed values are in the descriptions and the server checks every call with the zod schema.

Segment 1 (#1461) is the issue intake poller; segment 3 covers the repo rules for the in-product agent.

## Verified

The GitHub facts were read from the REST docs first ([p5a2-api-notes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-api-notes.txt)), and the list responses captured from this repository as test fixtures (`apps/server/test/fixtures/github-reads/`, copies in `docs/verify/1406/fixtures-p5a2/`).

Old leg, the new tests against unchanged sources ([p5a2-red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-red.txt)):

```
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
      Tests  39 failed | 23 passed (62)
```

Every new test fails and every existing test in those files passes. Re-run with the round 2 test set against the same sources ([p5a2-red-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/2b816b60679ede7ea19fbc2aa844222f38e11f9e/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-red-2.txt)): 43 failed, 24 passed of 67. The one new test that passes on main is the daemon-compatibility guard added in `59bc0e8` (chief parameters use only `type` and `description`), which main already satisfies; mutation M27 turns it red. New leg ([p5a2-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-green.txt)), across github-reads, mcp-face, the shared chief-tools tests, the daemon's `claude-t4-tools`, github-issues and ci-loop:

```
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  124 passed (124)
```

The gate run found one failure mode the plan had not listed: an `enum` in a chief parameter breaks the daemon's converter for every chief tool (the existing `claude-t4-tools` test went red); `59bc0e8` keeps chief parameters to `type` and `description`, recorded in the same file.

Each of 27 mutations, one rule undone at a time, turns a test red ([p5a2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-mutations.txt)): the team check, the repoKind, shape and dot-segment checks, an anonymous fallback, the cipher error, pull requests kept in issues, a body passed through, the task marker's team and case, the size and string bounds, format and control characters, each error class, the timeout and its signal, malformed bodies and entries, MCP keeping the stub or an optional `projectId`, the data note in the descriptions, and an `enum` back in a chief parameter.

The real server on `127.0.0.1:8796` with a scratch `PACMAN_HOME`, called through the MCP face over HTTP and reading this repository ([p5a2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-live.txt)): `issues` dropped pull requests, set `taskId` on the issue a scratch task was made from, and answered `perPage: 30` for a request of 100; `pull_requests` and `workflow_runs` (branch `main`, status `success`) returned real data; a bad status, a project that is not on GitHub and a missing `projectId` each came back as an error result. The chief face needs a daemon and a model to run live, so it is covered by the same function through `executeChiefTool` in the tests. In this container GitHub requests go through a proxy that authenticates them itself, so the live run used a dummy stored token: it shows the reads, bounds and filtering against real responses, and the team-token path (lookup, decryption, the 409 and the absent connection) is shown by the fake-GitHub tests.

Gates at `59bc0e8` ([gates-p5a2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a2.txt)): `pnpm lint` (1 existing info in `apps/web`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2464 with one failure, the root-only `runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败" case. `/simplify` folded the three list URLs into one helper and reused existing types ([p5a2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/10898214ef3ab5f3357accbe08b7f59450c87bfb/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-reviews.txt)); `/code-review` found nothing at `e92b20d` and `59bc0e8`. `/security-review` (AGENTS.md: `mcp-face.ts` is on its list): the first attempt could not run because this clone had no `origin/HEAD`, and `p5a2-reviews.txt` records the hand review done instead. With `origin/HEAD` set, the skill ran on `origin/HEAD...HEAD` at `1089821` ([p5a2-security-review.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/2b816b60679ede7ea19fbc2aa844222f38e11f9e/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-security-review.txt), its report verbatim; its file:line references do not match the files at `1089821`, so follow its paths by function name) and reported no finding at its confidence threshold; it traced cross-team reads, path and query injection, SQL parameters, token or URL leaks in errors, and third-party text reaching the model, and checked the committed evidence for token patterns.

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 (go at `1089821`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1467-run1-1089821.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/2b816b60679ede7ea19fbc2aa844222f38e11f9e/docs/verify/1406/pr-gate-1467-run1-1089821.json)), at `a5bf7ed` ([p5a2-mutations-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/2b816b60679ede7ea19fbc2aa844222f38e11f9e/docs/verify/1406/p5a2-mutations-2.txt), [gates-p5a2-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/2b816b60679ede7ea19fbc2aa844222f38e11f9e/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a2-2.txt)). Only a `SecretBoxError` from the token lookup becomes the 409 that asks to reconnect GitHub; a SQLite error or any other error reaches the caller as itself. A test spies on `AbortSignal.timeout` through the chief face and holds the timeout each GitHub read gets to at most `REMOTE_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` minus 3 s (the constant the daemon relay uses, from `@pacman/shared`), and a timeout while reading a response body is reported as a timeout (504), not as a malformed response. Spec 02 §7.2 now says the MCP `issues`, `pull_requests` and `workflow_runs` read GitHub for a project of the caller's team and need `projectId` (the same sentence also had `attachment` and chief `run_review` as stubs; both are corrected). Four mutations (the bare catch back, every token error propagated, ten times the timeout at the use site, a body-read timeout reported as malformed) are each caught; the last two survive the round 1 tests. github-reads has 39 tests; the four-file set passes 83 of 83. Gates: `pnpm lint` (1 existing info), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2468 with the one root-only runner-brief failure. `/code-review` on the round found nothing (that run is not archived).

## Upstream

No dependency is added. The endpoints are GitHub REST `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`, `/pulls` and `/actions/runs` (parameters, the 100-per-page maximum, the `pull_request` marker on issues, the run status values and rate-limit responses are quoted with URLs in `p5a2-api-notes.txt`). A fine-grained token needs issues, pull requests and actions read.

## Risk

Two-way door. The three tools change from empty results to real reads for the caller's team; an MCP client that called them with `{}` now gets an input error instead of an empty list, and a call naming a hosted or local project gets a 409 "not GitHub-backed" error on both faces instead of an empty list with a note. Each call costs one GitHub request on the team's token.

Found during this segment's security pass and left for #1466, fixed in #1468, because they are outside this diff: `isGithubRepoRef` accepts `.` and `..` as owner or repo, so a `githubRepo` of `../user` rewrites the path of the existing GitHub reads with the team token (these new tools refuse such a row); and `requireProjectRow` in chief-tools.ts and mcp-face.ts has no team check (latent on single-team installs). Saved chief memories reach the chief system prompt each turn, unchanged by this diff. Issue and PR titles written by outside authors now reach the chief as tool results; the descriptions mark them as third-party data, bodies are not returned, and format characters are removed, but nothing stops the model from acting on a title. Fencing that text in the chief's prompt is segment 3 of #1406 (repo rules for the in-product agent). Neither is a finding of the `/security-review` run on this diff: the first is outside it, and the skill's rules exclude user-controlled text reaching a model.

The patch is 5,722 lines (2,427 outside `docs/verify/`) across 29 files and touches `apps/server/src/services/mcp-face.ts` (ADR 0021 D4 class ⑤), so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Chief and MCP `issues`, `pull_requests`, `workflow_runs` return real data from a fake GitHub (`github-reads.test.ts`); the MCP face also from this repository (`p5a2-live.txt`)
- [x] Team gate, project gate, token handling, bounds, data framing and error classes held by tests; 27 of 27 mutations caught, and 4 of 4 in round 2 (`p5a2-mutations.txt`, `p5a2-mutations-2.txt`)
- [x] `/security-review` run at `1089821` (no finding at its threshold, `p5a2-security-review.txt`); the two issues outside the diff filed as #1466
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case (`gates-p5a2.txt`, `gates-p5a2-2.txt`)

## Issues

Part of #1406, segment 2 of 3. The last segment carries the closing line for #1406; this squash body has no closing keyword for it.

Squash with this message:

```
server(1406): chief and MCP GitHub read tools read GitHub (#1467)

The chief and MCP tools issues, pull_requests and workflow_runs read
GitHub for a project of the caller's team with the team token, through
one shared implementation (services/github-reads.ts). Bounded pages and
strings, format and control characters removed, no issue or PR bodies,
short error results per failure class, 6 s timeout; only a
SecretBoxError becomes the reconnect 409. MCP projectId is
required, as on chief; chief parameters stay type and description only
so installed daemons keep their tool converter working.

Part of #1406 (segment 2 of 3).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012odUHNQRa4CWjzR22iWH8s
```

A registry mistake (missing script, tsx case without `cwd`) fails before anything runs, `--dry-run` included. A case that needs the stack runs `doctor` first, stops if doctor fails, and passes the stack's `ports.json` ports to the probe as `VERIFY_PORT` / `VERIFY_WEB_PORT` and the run directory doctor checked as `VERIFY_RUN_DIR` (a different `VERIFY_PORT` in the environment is refused, so a probe never drives another lane's stack). Without `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_DIR` each drive writes to a new `.claude/verify-evidence/--/` in the main checkout (also when this `vp.mjs` sits in a worktree, which is deleted with its evidence, #345), made after doctor passes and never an existing directory (`-2`, `-3` instead), because several probes default their evidence into `docs/verify//` or into `scripts/`. mergedPulls.title: server(1404): merge gate S1, patch digest, D4 path classes, raw evidence links
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment S1 of #1404 (bootstrap phase P3, the merge readiness gate). The segment plan and the design choices are in the ticket comment from the design-panel workflow (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1404#issuecomment-6304303150). This segment adds shared vocabulary and three pure server functions. Nothing calls them yet.

- `packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts` holds the merge policies (`human | shadow | autonomous`), the status context `pacman/merge-gate`, the gate limits (800 lines, 40 files, compare cap 300, fix rounds 2, rounds 4), the digest version `pd2`, the evidence prefix `docs/verify/` and the executable extensions. It also holds the D4 path lists of ADR 0021 (the auto-merge set, protected classes ① to ③ and ⑤, the gate's own source as class ④) and the compare file shape. The path lists are the same as `PROTECTED` and `AUTO_MERGE` in `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` on #1410.
- `apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/digest.ts` has `computePatchDigest(files, {expectedFileCount})`. It drops entries under `docs/verify/`, but keeps a rename when only one of its two names is under that directory. It sorts JSON tuples `[status, filename, previous_filename, sha, patchSha]` by code unit and returns `pd2:` plus the sha256; `patchSha` is the sha256 of the file's patch text, so a branch that merges main and keeps its own version in a conflict changes the digest even though its blobs do not. 300 or more files, or a count that differs from the PR's `changed_files`, gives `truncated` / `count-mismatch` and no digest. A null sha on anything but a removal gives `null-sha`, and a patch with nothing outside `docs/verify/` gives no digest (there is no code to bind). `countedFiles` / `countedLines` feed the 800-line / 40-file caps and count the whole patch, evidence included (ADR 0021 D4 as amended on #1410); a rename counts as two files, as pr-gate's `--no-renames` list does, and lines are compare's additions plus deletions, so a pure rename adds 0 lines. `compareFilesFromResponse` turns the REST body into those entries, with `patchSha` set when GitHub sent a non-empty `patch` (null otherwise), or null when the shape is wrong (a negative count, or a rename or copy without `previous_filename`, included).
- `apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/paths.ts` has `classifyPaths(files, ticketRef)`. It matches both names of a rename against the D4 globs with the same glob syntax and case rule as pr-gate: matching that grants auto-merge folds ASCII case only, matching that protects folds Unicode case, and a protected directory glob also matches the bare directory name. A name with a character outside pr-gate's `SAFE_PATH` whitelist (a line break, a space, a tab) counts as protected, because `.` in the glob regex does not cross a line terminator while `*` does, so `apps/x\ny/src/CLAUDE.md` would otherwise read as auto-mergeable. It returns the protected paths, the gate-source subset, the paths outside the auto-merge set, deleted tests (directory and suffix matched without case, as pr-gate does; every rename of a test counts, as pr-gate's `--no-renames` list does, including a rename inside a test directory to a name the runner does not collect), writes into another ticket's evidence directory, executable files (`.jsx` and `.tsx` included) added or changed under `docs/verify/`, with the evidence prefix matched without case, and `opaque`: names outside `docs/verify/` (matched with case, as the digest does) whose entry has no patch. GitHub sends no patch for a binary file, a very large diff or a pure rename, and compare cannot tell a binary rename from a text one, so all three count (D4 sends a binary file outside the evidence to a person).
- `apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/evidence-link.ts` has `parseRawEvidenceLinks(body, {owner, repo, ticketRef})`. A link counts when it pins a 40-hex lowercase sha and points into this repo's `docs/verify/<ticket>/`; every other raw link goes to `others`. Links inside HTML comments are skipped, as in `scripts/pr-evidence-gate.py`, and an unclosed comment hides the rest of the body only where it opens an HTML block (at a line start), as GitHub renders it; a comment is replaced by a space, so a URL split by a comment is not joined into a link GitHub would not render. The parser is linear: a 65,536-character adversarial body took 3.7 s before round 5 and about 1 ms now. Empty comments (`<!-->`) end where GitHub ends them. Trailing punctuation and backticks after a link are not part of its path, nor is a query string or fragment (`?raw=true`, `#L3`); one file is recorded once, by its decoded sha and path, and a malformed percent escape goes to `others`.

The fixture `apps/server/test/fixtures/merge-gate-compare-sample.json` (copy in `docs/verify/1404/compare-sample.json`) is a real read-only compare response (`52d2cdc...b4b1f96`, `per_page=1`, no token) with URL fields removed and each `patch` cut to a placeholder where GitHub sent one (38 entries; the 20 PNGs got none). Two facts from it shaped the code. Removed entries carry the old blob sha, not null. Files under `docs/verify/` include `.mjs` scripts. The tests read the copy under `apps/server/test/fixtures/`, so a change to the input they check changes the digest; a fixture under `docs/verify/` would not.

## Verified

Old leg: the three test files on this branch before the modules existed ([s1-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9c640f5eb0c6c98b68018b6015e05a940d7366e8/docs/verify/1404/s1-red-green.txt)):

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/merge-gate-{digest,paths,evidence-link}.test.ts
 FAIL  test/merge-gate-digest.test.ts
Error: Cannot find module '../src/services/merge-gate/digest.js'
 FAIL  test/merge-gate-evidence-link.test.ts
Error: Cannot find module '../src/services/merge-gate/evidence-link.js'
 FAIL  test/merge-gate-paths.test.ts
Error: Cannot find module '../src/services/merge-gate/paths.js'
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
```

New leg:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/merge-gate-{digest,paths,evidence-link}.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  58 passed (58)
```

The tests cover the failure modes from the design: a code rename into `docs/verify/` hidden from the digest, a protected file renamed away, tab and newline in file names, a null sha, a list cut at 300, case variants, nested `scripts/` and configs, a test deleted by renaming, other tickets' evidence, executable evidence, and raw links with the wrong repo, ticket, short or uppercase sha, a branch name, `..`, or inside a comment.

Each of 15 mutations of the three modules turns at least one test red ([s1-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9c640f5eb0c6c98b68018b6015e05a940d7366e8/docs/verify/1404/s1-mutations.txt), with the patch of each):

```
digest: rename into evidence excluded         1 failed | 57 passed (58)
digest: tab-joined tuples                     1 failed | 57 passed (58)
digest: unsorted                              2 failed | 56 passed (58)
paths: case-sensitive                         2 failed | 56 passed (58)
paths: previous name ignored                  2 failed | 56 passed (58)
link: comments scanned                        1 failed | 57 passed (58)
...
```

The fixture's expected digest `pd1:ddf04cd2…7655f` (36 files kept, 22 evidence files dropped, 846 lines) was computed by a separate Python script written from ADR 0021 D3, not copied from the TypeScript output ([digest-crosscheck.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9c640f5eb0c6c98b68018b6015e05a940d7366e8/docs/verify/1404/digest-crosscheck.txt), [compare-sample.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9c640f5eb0c6c98b68018b6015e05a940d7366e8/docs/verify/1404/compare-sample.json)).

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 on this PR (head `9c640f5`), at `11ecbde` ([s1-r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/11ecbded3d9ec9569c02858efa64fbd7aa56680f/docs/verify/1404/s1-r2-red-green.txt)). The run found two holes in `classifyPaths`: a name with a line break escaped the protected globs, and a test renamed inside a test directory to a name the runner does not collect was not counted as deleted. Its suggestions added the case-free evidence prefix, `.jsx` / `.tsx`, no digest for an evidence-only patch, link punctuation, the unclosed comment, and the fixture move. The round 2 test files against the S1 code at `9c640f5`:

```
     × 名字里有换行、回车、空格或其它白名单外字符：一律算保护（与 pr-gate SAFE_PATH 同一白名单）
     × 测试的任何改名都算删了原测试（与 pr-gate 的 --no-renames 一致），含测试目录里改成不被收集的名字
     × 证据目录前缀换大小写也照样检查别票与可执行文件；.tsx / .jsx 算可执行
     × 空文件列表：摘要不可得（没有可绑定的补丁）
     × 只有证据的补丁：证据之外没有文件，摘要不可得
     × 链接后面紧跟的标点与反引号不算进路径
     × 没闭合的 HTML 注释吞掉后文（GitHub 不渲染），其中的链接不算
      Tests  7 failed | 61 passed (68)
```

At `11ecbde` the three files pass 69 of 69 (the 69th, a link after a closed comment, was added when the first mutation pass left `link: comments scanned` alive; it passes on both sides). Each of 21 mutations turns at least one test red ([s1-mutations-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/11ecbded3d9ec9569c02858efa64fbd7aa56680f/docs/verify/1404/s1-mutations-2.txt); it restates every pattern, since three of round 1's no longer match the formatted source). Gates ([gates-s1-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/11ecbded3d9ec9569c02858efa64fbd7aa56680f/docs/verify/1404/gates-s1-2.txt)): lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse and e2e:affected pass; `vitest run --changed` has the same one root-only failure as round 1, described below.

mergedPulls.body:
## What

Phase P0 of the bootstrap loop: pacman writes its own PRs and merges them. Answers #1401.

- `docs/spec/28-自举闭环-自写自合.md` is the plan: target state, gaps at `af161e3`, decisions D1-D7, phases P0-P8 with failure modes and acceptance, premortem, metrics, the goal-mode runbook (local and cloud variants), the workflow orchestration (§7.5) and the progress ledger (§8).
- `docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md` records the product decisions D1-D6. `project.mergePolicy` is `human | shadow | autonomous` and the default is `human`. Under `human`, ADR 0018 ("the merge action stays with a human") and the two #1256 blocks (`MERGE_HUMAN_ONLY_COPY` in `chief-tools.ts` and `mcp-face.ts`) hold unchanged. On the autonomous path the server merges through REST with the `sha` parameter; a merge clicked in pacman goes through the same server call. Verdicts bind to a `patchDigest` computed from `compare/{base}...{headSha}` without `docs/verify/**`. D4 is default deny: only product source and tests (`apps/*/src`, `apps/*/test`, `apps/*/e2e`, `packages/*/src`, `packages/*/test`, `integration/test`) and `docs/verify/**` may merge without a person, and only outside the protected classes, which match at any depth and ignore case (CI and hooks; files that steer agents, including `AGENTS*.md`, `CLAUDE*.md`, `.claude/`, `.pi/` and `.cursor/`; gate scripts and the configs that decide what a check covers, `.gitattributes` included; migrations and the supply chain; the merge readiness gate's own source). Deleted tests (directory and suffix matched without case), binary files outside `docs/verify/`, and patches over 800 lines or 40 files (the whole patch, evidence included) also go to the user; the line count takes attributes from the empty tree, so a committed `.gitattributes` cannot zero it, and a NUL byte that makes git treat a source file as binary sends the PR to a person. The gate's own source lives only in the three paths D4 class ④ names.
- `docs/adr/0018-多agent团队三层与机器能力闸.md` gets a two-line revision pointer under its status line. The body is unchanged.
- `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` is the pre-merge gate the bootstrap session runs before it merges or asks for a merge (spec 28 §7.5). Five reviewers read the PR at one head SHA; blocking findings get two skeptics each, at most four skeptics in all (a third finding keeps go false without them), and a finding is withdrawn only when both its skeptics answer on that SHA and both refute. The script decides D4 routing itself from `changedFiles`, `deletedFiles`, `linesChanged` and `binaryFiles` (the `- -` rows of the same numstat). The safety reviewer takes all four from git without seeing the caller's list, so a list built without `--no-renames` or `core.quotePath=false`, or a low line count from the writing session, cannot hide a D4 case. Subagents are told GitHub is read-only, and the evidence reviewer and its skeptics run nothing from a PR whose head is a fork. `.gitignore` adds `!.claude/workflows/` to the `.claude/` allowlist.
- `scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs` runs the script with stub agents to check its deterministic part without spending subagents (85 cases), and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs it in the check job.
- `docs/pr-review.md` records the four places pr-gate departs from the human review steps (no label or comment, a JSON verdict; a detached checkout in its own worktree; private refs named by head; PR comments fetched with a filter that keeps only repository members). Spec 28 §7.5 pins auto-merge to the head pr-gate judged.
- The §8 ledger carries the tickets #1401-#1409 (P0-P8) and, for P1 to P3, the PRs in flight (#1411, #1414, #1420, #1421), since the phase branches cut from main do not have spec 28 until this PR merges. P7 and P8 wait for a long-lived host. D7 now says what §7.4 implies: every phase PR edits §8 under `docs/spec/`, outside the auto-merge set, so each one waits for a user merge; the round summary's merge list is a report, not a question under AGENTS.md's `needs-decision` rule.

## Upstream

pr-gate uses the Workflow tool's own orchestration (`pipeline`, `parallel`, `agent` with a JSON schema) and adds no runtime code to the product. The ADR and the plan add no mechanism; the endpoints they name (REST merge with `sha`, commit status, compare) are GitHub REST features that the phase tickets check against the official docs before use.

## Risk

Two-way door. ADR 0021 sets the default `mergePolicy` to `human`, so no project changes behavior until a later PR adds the column and someone turns it on. This PR routes to a user merge under its own D4: it touches `.github/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `scripts/**`, `AGENTS.md` (one line: the pr-gate worktree exception to the no-checkout rule), `docs/pr-review.md` and `.gitignore`, and it changes 6,268 lines across 43 files. Default deny sends more PRs to a person than either list did: docs-only PRs outside `docs/verify/`, `apps/web/public/`, `integration/eval/`, root files. That is the intended side of the trade; a path that should merge alone is added to the auto-merge set in a PR the user merges. The §8 merger column names the user for P1 to P3, each with its reason. The new CI step is pure node and runs in under a second. `.gitignore` gains one allowlist line; `git check-ignore -v .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` printed nothing after it. pr-gate's evidence dimension and its skeptics check out the PR head in their own worktrees and run commands quoted in the PR with this session's credentials; spec 28 §7.5 limits pr-gate to PRs this session wrote, and the evidence prompts tell the reviewer and its skeptics to check out, install and run nothing from a fork head, to read one with `git show` and `git diff` only, to run every checkout, fetch and ref cleanup with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, and to install a same-repo head with `HUSKY=0` (prompt rules, not code; run 10 showed that a relative `core.hooksPath` would otherwise run hooks a fork commits). That checkout is the one place pr-gate departs from docs/pr-review.md step 4 ("不切分支看 diff"), which CLAUDE.md calls a hard rule; it is the §7.5 design the user authorized when allowing pr-gate, it never touches the shared working tree the rule protects, and the PR adds a section to docs/pr-review.md naming it. Code that implements merge authority today (the #1256 block in chief-tools.ts, AGENT_TOOL_SWITCHES, persona prompts) sits in the auto-merge set under D4 as written (mcp-face.ts is now class ⑤); run 6 noted it, and the P3 and P4 gates are where merges get decided, so this PR leaves the class list as it is; the P4 plan on #1405 asks you whether to move the merge writer into class 4. ADR 0021's premortem names an agent changing tests to pass its own gate, and D4 counts only deleted tests: a test weakened in place is left to the tests dimension of this gate and to the P3 review perspectives. Three of this branch's commit subjects carry no ticket; the squash message under Issues is the one to use. The pr-gate worktree exception in AGENTS.md and the reading in spec 28 D7 that a list of PRs waiting for your merge is a report, not a question, both come from spec 28 §7.4, §7.5 and D7, which your /goal prompt for this session confirmed; merging this PR keeps them.

### P0 · Rulings on disk (docs only)
### P1 · Verification CLI convergence (the video's Control Glass)
### P2 · GitHub PR surface + merge reconciliation

- **Failure modes**: GitHub 429 / 404 / network error → fail-open, retry next round (ci-loop discipline); a human advances the phase within the network window → re-read before writing; the same PR pointed at by two builds (#1217 guard); merge returns 405 (not mergeable) → re-evaluate next round, no retry bombing.
### P3 · Merge-readiness gate (patch-bound verdicts + automated review / verification + chief go/no-go)

- The pure function `mergeReadiness(build) → {ready, blockers[]}`, whose blockers cover at least: policy is `human`; autonomy paused; the PR is not open or is a draft; `mergeable_state ≠ clean` (`has_hooks` counts as `clean`; `unstable` is passed only when everything unpassed is the gate's own statuses) or a non-required check failed; the required checks not all green at the current head; `pr-evidence` not green; a verification verdict missing / failed / digest stale; any review with a blocking or a stale digest; chief has not gone or its digest is stale; a D4 protected path or size cap hit; tests deleted; the todo's `sourceRef` resolves to no issue number (D2 cannot assemble `closes #N`); the body's raw evidence links do not point at this branch's `docs/verify/<ticket>/` (the AGENTS.md pre-merge verification rule).
### P4 · Autonomous merge (policy + executor + brakes)
- After merge: P2 reconciliation pushes the todo to `done`; the commit message's `closes #N` closes the issue; `scripts/cleanup-merged-branches.sh` cleans the branch.
### P5 · Autonomous intake + internalizing the repo rules

- **P5a intake**: issue polling (5 minutes, scheduler family; opt-in, only enabled with `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` as `1` / `true` / `yes`, default off), filtered per D5 (the tag has no unlabeled after its newest labeled event, and the tagger is triage or above on the repo; a labeled event carrying `performed_via_github_app` — tagged via a GitHub App — is not claimed. This can only recognize GitHub Apps: tags applied with an OAuth App token or a PAT look on the event exactly like that account tagging by hand, and cannot be intercepted. OAuth App tokens include the token `gh auth login` obtains for itself and the team's GitHub connection token (exchanged from a self-registered GitHub OAuth App) — pacman hands it to git with the step (git's own hooks also run in this environment), and to the repo's `.agents/setup` / `.agents/resume` hooks; any agent step that can change those hooks can get it; pacman's agent steps can also directly use the machine's logged-in `gh`. Both paths can tag as the corresponding account and feed the intake), import (`sourceRef` 409 dedupe) → `orchestrateTodo`; a project-level in-flight cap (default 3). The webhook's `pacman` trigger (#1459, effective whether or not intake is on) follows the same D5 and the same cap: the tagger is taken from the event's `sender`, imported only if triage or above on the repo (same permission read and same cache as the poller), and the current in-flight count includes imports still waiting on the GitHub read; no sender, the sender is not a GitHub account name, the sender is below triage, the permission read fails or rate-limits, the project is full, the team has no usable token, the project's stored githubRepo is not owner/repo, or the issue is not found on GitHub — none of these import; a log line records the reason code, and all reply 202 (a rejection does not feed GitHub retries; the three tagger-permission-class rejections all reply the same one line, never saying which kind or which account. This only removes the permission conclusion from the reply; whether the import proceeds afterwards still reveals whether the tagger qualifies; remediation of a leaked URL token is still revocation). The webhook payload has no `performed_via_github_app`, so a `pacman` tag applied via a GitHub App still imports; left to a later phase. chief's `issues` / `pull_requests` / `workflow_runs` become real reads.

- **Internalizing the repo rules**: measure once in a daemon worktree — `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` natively read by the engine (spec 24), `.claude/skills/pr-pacman` and `verify-pacman` usable, `pnpm lint` / `typecheck` / `spec:parse` runnable, the body passes `pr-evidence`. Whatever does not hold is patched into the run brief (spec 24) or the Implementer persona copy. The daemon `commitAll`'s in-branch commit form is `<kind>: <title>`, different from the repo rule `<scope>(<ticket>): <subject>`. The message squashed into main depends on who initiates the merge: the autonomous path takes the D2 server-assembled message; clicking merge inside pacman also merges via server REST (#1403); when no message is passed, GitHub follows the repo settings (single commit: that commit's message; multiple: the PR title plus each commit's message), so a single-commit PR carries `<kind>: <title>` into main. Hence the alignment is server-side: the REST merge uniformly passes `commit_title` (the PR title) plus D2's body last line; in-branch commits are unchanged; the PR title itself is aligned to the repo rules by P5.

### 7.4 Cloud-session variant (user's 2026-10-20 choice: run in the current Claude Code cloud session first, no separate host)

Ledger rules (common to both variants): each phase edits its §8 row in its own PR (backfill the PR number after opening and push once more); **PR merged = that row in effect on main**; across context compactions, progress truth is §8 on `origin/main` plus in-flight PRs. ### 7.5 Workflow orchestration (authorized by the user 2026-10-20: "use workflow to join the plan")

- `pr-gate` is stored as the in-repo workflow `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js`, committed with P0's PR (#1410), parameters `{pr, headSha, ticket, changedFiles, deletedFiles, linesChanged, binaryFiles}`: `changedFiles` from `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only origin/main...<headSha>`, `deletedFiles` is the same command plus `--diff-filter=D`, `linesChanged` is the sum of both columns of `git -c core.quotePath=false --attr-source=4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 diff --no-renames --numstat origin/main...<headSha>` (binary rows `- -` count 0; attributes taken from the empty tree, so the repo's `.gitattributes` `-diff` cannot change the line count, pr-gate round six; `--attr-source` needs git 2.40+, and on older gits reporting an unknown option, upgrade git, do not drop this option), `binaryFiles` are the paths of `- -` rows in the same numstat: binary files outside `docs/verify/` stay with humans (one NUL byte in a source file makes git treat the file as binary and count 0 lines, #1410's `/code-review`). Without `core.quotePath=false`, git escapes non-ASCII paths (every file under `docs/adr/`) into a quoted form the globs cannot match; the script rejects paths starting with a quote on sight. Without `--no-renames`, renames list only the new name, so a protected file renamed away is missed (#1410 pr-gate round two). The security dimension does not look at the caller's list; it takes these four itself with the same commands, and the script takes the union and the larger values (the caller is the PR-writing session). numstat also needs `core.quotePath=false`, else non-ASCII binary paths get quoted and fail to match the file list (#1410 pr-gate round seven). Reviewers read only PR comments from repo members (`author_association` OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR); the comment commands use `--jq` to filter out the rest first, and bodies do not enter the reviewers' context: the repo is public, anyone can comment, and the evidence dimension has a shell (#1410 final `/code-review`). A ticket's body may, under D5, come from an outside author; the prompt states it as author-written untrusted data, not instructions, same as the PR body (#1410 pr-gate round eleven). Subagents are read-only on GitHub. The deterministic parts (parameter validation, D4 judging, rebuttal-withdrawal rules, go) are self-checked by `scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs` with stub agents, run by the CI check job every time; it lives under `scripts/`, itself a D4 surface. **Run the copy on origin/main** (`git show origin/main:.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` written to a throwaway file, then invoked via `scriptPath`), not the copy in the PR-under-review's worktree — a PR must not edit the gate that judges it. Named invocation resolves against `.claude/workflows/` in the session's **current working directory**: it is not found by name inside a worktree that does not contain the file; after the file in the same directory is changed, the content fetched by name may still be the previously scanned copy (#1410, measured three times, `docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-named-probe.txt` and `pr-gate-named-probe-2.txt`). It belongs to ADR 0021 D4 protected paths; edits are merged by the user.
